{"body":"## Scope

Design and build the CLI sanitizer that scrubs raw Claude Code session JSONL files for safe publication. This is the security boundary for the entire project — without it, all fixtures must be synthetic.

The sanitizer is also a standalone artifact with its own potential audience: anyone who wants to share Claude Code session data without leaking secrets, file paths, or personal identifiers.

**Roadmap reference:** See [`.claude/specs/roadmap-v0.md` (W2)](https://github.com/real-user/claude-code-sessions/blob/main/.claude/specs/roadmap-v0.md#w2--sanitizer-design--v0-implementation) for full narrative context.

## Phasing

This epic has two phases:

1. **Phase 1 — Design PRD** (first deliverable when this epic activates):
   - Write a thorough PRD at `.claude/specs/prd-sanitizer.md`
   - The PRD should be **verbose and comprehensive**: design rationale, alternatives considered, decision history — not just the final spec. We are early-stage and want rich historical documentation.
   - The PRD must address every open question listed in [`tooling/sanitizer/README.md` "Dependencies on this scaffold"](https://github.com/real-user/claude-code-sessions/blob/main/tooling/sanitizer/README.md) section:
     1. Yaml-configured rule sets vs. code-defined rules
     2. Sidecar substitution dictionaries (reviewable but leaky) vs. rule-level counts only
     3. Statistical jitter granularity (per-field, per-message, per-session)
     4. Integration with the fixture-validator (re-scan vs. trust the sidecar)
   - Additional open questions from the roadmap:
     - Should the sanitizer publish as its own PyPI package, or live only in this repo? (Roadmap says in-repo only for v0.)
     - Where does the secret-pattern library live — copied from AgentFluent, or referenced as a dependency?

2. **Phase 2 — Implementation** (after PRD is accepted):
   - Python CLI (uv-managed), usable as `ccs-sanitize <input.jsonl> -o <output.jsonl>` or equivalent
   - Layered rules: paths -> identifiers -> secrets -> optional jitter
   - `.scrubbed` sidecar output with rule-level counts and configurable substitution detail
   - Fail-closed: any rule error aborts; no partial scrubs
   - Test suite covering known-bad inputs

## Prerequisites

- **Secret-detection hooks must be ported to this repo before any real session data lands.** See the standalone issue for porting AgentFluent's `block_secret_reads.py` + `detect_secrets_in_output.py`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] PRD at `.claude/specs/prd-sanitizer.md` is thorough, covers all open questions, and documents alternatives considered
- [ ] CLI implemented per the PRD design
- [ ] Outputs `.scrubbed` sidecar meeting the format described in `tooling/sanitizer/README.md`
- [ ] Test suite covers known-bad inputs from `tests/fixtures/`
- [ ] At least one real session successfully sanitized and committed to `fixtures/sanitized/` with sidecar

## Child stories

_Stories will be filed when this epic activates. Phase 1 (PRD) is the first story._

## Status

**Stub** — this epic is scoped but not yet active. Stories will be expanded when W1 (first post) is underway or complete.

1	# PRD — Session JSONL Sanitizer (`ccs-sanitize`)
2	
3	**Status:** Design (Phase 1 of W2). Implementation has not started.
4	**Owner:** Real Name
5	**Roadmap item:** [W2 — Sanitizer design + v0 implementation](roadmap-v0.md#w2--sanitizer-design--v0-implementation)
6	**Tracking issue:** [#1 — Epic: Sanitizer design + v0 implementation](https://github.com/real-user/claude-code-sessions/issues/1)
7	**Created:** 2026-05-29
8	**Last updated:** 2026-05-29
9	
10	> This PRD is deliberately verbose. Per the epic, we are early-stage and want the
11	> design rationale, the alternatives considered, and the decision history recorded
12	> alongside the final spec — not just the spec. Sections marked **Decision** record a
13	> resolved question; sections marked **Alternatives** record what was rejected and why.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 1. Purpose
18	
19	`ccs-sanitize` is the CLI tool that scrubs raw Claude Code session JSONL files so they
20	can be committed to this repository (as `fixtures/sanitized/`) or shared publicly by
21	anyone. It is the **security boundary** of the whole project: without it, every fixture
22	must be synthetic, which limits which real-world phenomena the blog can illustrate
23	(a multi-hour real subagent trace, real token-accounting shapes, real tool-error cascades).
24	
25	The tool has two audiences:
26	
27	1. **This repo.** Produces the `.scrubbed` sidecar that gates `fixtures/sanitized/`
28	   (see [CLAUDE.md → Security posture](../../CLAUDE.md) and
29	   [fixtures conventions](../../CLAUDE.md)).
30	2. **Standalone users.** Anyone who wants to share a Claude Code session — in a bug
31	   report, a blog post, a gist — without leaking secrets, file paths, or personal
32	   identifiers. "Sanitize your Claude Code session before sharing" is a real, unmet need,
33	   and the tool is designed to stand on its own (see [§12 Packaging](#12-packaging)).
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 2. Background: what makes raw session JSONL dangerous
38	
39	The [data dictionary](../../reference/data-dictionary.md) documents the format in full.
40	For sanitization purposes, the dangerous surfaces are:
41	
42	| Surface | Where it lives | Risk |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| **Home directory & username** | `cwd`, `toolUseResult.file`/`filePath`, the project slug (`-home-USER-project`), `transcript_path` echoes | Leaks the OS username and directory layout on every line. |
45	| **Absolute file paths** | `cwd`, tool inputs (`file_path`, `command`), `toolUseResult` path fields, `structuredPatch` | Leaks project structure, internal names, sometimes employer/client identity. |
46	| **Project slug** | the directory name *and* `cwd` on every line | Encodes home dir + project path together; must be scrubbed consistently with `cwd`. |
47	| **Identifiers** | git author email, `gitBranch` (often `feature/JIRA-123-...`), prompt text | PII and internal ticket/project names. |
48	| **Secrets** | Bash `stdout`/`stderr`, file contents via `Read`, env dumps, prompt text | API keys, tokens — the catastrophic case. Patterns in [`.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py`](../../.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py). |
49	| **Whole-file backups** | `file-history-snapshot.snapshot.trackedFileBackups` — full pre-edit file contents indexed by absolute path | **Highest-risk field in the format.** Holds entire files (configs, source, possibly `.env` snapshots). v0 **drops these lines wholesale** rather than scrub arbitrary contents — see [§6b](#6b-line-type-stripping-and-traversal-depth) and [D-7](#decision-d-7--v0-drops-high-risk-line-types). |
50	| **Tool inputs** | `tool_use.input` — Bash `command`, Agent `prompt`, MCP tool inputs (arbitrary schemas) | Commands and prompts carry paths, secrets, and free-text PII. Reached only via structural traversal ([§6b](#6b-line-type-stripping-and-traversal-depth)). |
51	| **Subagent / free-text prompts** | `toolUseResult.prompt`, `SubagentStart.initial_prompt` | Concentrated free-text PII — the full prompt handed to a subagent. |
52	| **Free-text prompts & tool output** | `message.content` (string and array shapes), `tool_result.content` | Arbitrary content. May contain names, company info, proprietary code. **Not reliably auto-scrubbable** — see [§4 Non-goals](#4-non-goals). |
53	| **Attachments** | `attachment` lines; image content blocks | Opaque to regex (binary/base64). v0 **drops `attachment` lines** — see [D-7](#decision-d-7--v0-drops-high-risk-line-types). |
54	| **Thinking signatures** | `thinking.signature` | High-entropy opaque blob; can false-positive on secret patterns. Replaced with a fixed placeholder (no analytical value in a fixture). |
55	| **Timestamps** | `timestamp` on most lines | Reveals working hours, session duration, cadence — a fingerprint. Addressed by jitter ([§9](#9-layer-4-jitter-deferred-to-v1-but-designed)), deferred to v1. |
56	| **UUIDs** | `uuid`, `parentUuid`, `sessionId`, `agentId`, `requestId`, `message.id`, `tool_use.id` | Not inherently sensitive (high-entropy random), but if remapped the conversation graph must stay linked. Remapping is **off by default** ([§8](#8-layer-2-identifiers)). |
57	
58	Two surfaces are **out of scope by design**: model IDs/versions (`message.model`, `version`)
59	and token-accounting numbers (`usage.*`) carry no PII and are analytically valuable, so the
60	sanitizer leaves them untouched (token counts are only perturbed by the deferred jitter layer,
61	and even then off by default).
62	
63	---
64	
65	## 3. Goals
66	
67	- **Fail-closed.** Any rule error, any malformed line, or any secret surviving to the
68	  output aborts the run with a non-zero exit and **no output file**. There is never a
69	  partial scrub.
70	- **No silent transforms.** The `.scrubbed` sidecar enumerates every category of change so
71	  a human reviewer can audit what happened — without the sidecar itself becoming a leak.
72	- **Deterministic.** Same input + same config → byte-identical output. This is what makes
73	  per-file runs safe (see [§7 consistency](#consistency-determinism-is-the-safety-property))
74	  and keeps committed fixtures git-stable.
75	- **Layered.** Independent rule layers (paths → identifiers → secrets → jitter) applied in a
76	  fixed order, each independently testable.
77	- **Versioned output.** Every sidecar records `sanitizer_version`; downstream consumers
78	  (the fixture-validator, sibling projects) can trust or distrust by version.
79	- **Standalone.** Usable with no dependency on this repo's layout or on AgentFluent/CodeFluent.
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 4. Non-goals
84	
85	These are **explicitly out of scope** and the PRD states them loudly because over-trusting
86	the sanitizer is the most likely way to leak data.
87	
88	- **The sanitizer is not a guarantee against all PII in free-text prompts.** It catches
89	  *structured* leaks — paths, configured identifiers, and secret *patterns*. It cannot catch
90	  "my name is Jane and I work at AcmeCorp" typed into a prompt. Mitigations: the sidecar
91	  drives human review, and the repo's standing policy keeps **synthetic the default**
92	  (per [CLAUDE.md fixtures](../../CLAUDE.md) — use sanitized "only when realistic data shape
93	  can't be reproduced synthetically").
94	- **No GUI / interactive review mode** (deferred; see [§14](#14-future-work-v1)).
95	- **No streaming sanitization of live sessions.** Operates on files at rest.
96	- **No automatic upload** to any destination. The tool writes local files; publishing is a
97	  separate, human-initiated step.
98	- **No reverse-mapping.** The scrub is one-way. The sidecar deliberately cannot reconstruct
99	  the original (see [§10](#10-the-scrubbed-sidecar)).
100	- **Jitter is designed but not implemented in v0** (see [§9](#9-layer-4-jitter-deferred-to-v1-but-designed)).
101	
102	---
103	
104	## 5. Design principles & the role of the post-scrub residual scan
105	
106	The single most important safety mechanism is the **residual secret scan**: after all
107	transform layers have run, the sanitizer re-runs the secret-pattern detector over the
108	*output*. If anything matches, a secret survived redaction (a bug, or a secret split across
109	a transform boundary, or an unknown encoding) — the run **aborts and writes nothing**.
110	
111	This means the design has two distinct secret interactions, and conflating them is a common
112	mistake:
113	
114	1. **Detection during scrub** (expected): secret patterns match in the input → redacted →
115	   counted in the sidecar. A secret match here is normal — it's the tool doing its job.
116	2. **Residual verification after scrub** (must be clean): the same patterns run over the
117	   output. A match here is a failure condition, not a normal event.
118	
119	The residual scan is also why the fixture-validator re-scans independently rather than
120	trusting the sidecar (see [§11](#11-fixture-validator-integration)) — defense in depth, the
121	same check enforced at two layers owned by two tools.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## 6. Architecture overview
126	
127	A line-oriented pipeline. Each JSONL line is parsed, passed through the ordered transform
128	layers, and re-serialized. The substitution table accumulates across lines so replacements
129	are **consistent within a file** (the same real home dir maps to the same placeholder on
130	line 1 and line 5,000).
131	
132	```
133	input.jsonl
134	   │
135	   ▼  parse line (fail-closed on malformed JSON)
136	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
137	│  Layer 1: paths        (deterministic remap) │
138	│  Layer 2: identifiers  (deterministic remap) │
139	│  Layer 3: secrets      (redact + count)      │
140	│  Layer 4: jitter       (DEFERRED to v1)      │
141	└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
142	   │  accumulate substitution table + counts
143	   ▼  (all lines processed)
144	residual secret scan over full output  ──► match? ABORT, no output
145	   │  clean
146	   ▼
147	atomic write: output.jsonl  +  output.jsonl.scrubbed
148	```
149	
150	Module layout (matches the [README's planned shape](../../tooling/sanitizer/README.md)):
151	
152	```
153	tooling/sanitizer/
154	├── pyproject.toml                 # uv-managed; entry point `ccs-sanitize`
155	├── src/ccs_sanitize/
156	│   ├── __init__.py
157	│   ├── cli.py                     # arg parsing, exit codes, atomic write
158	│   ├── pipeline.py                # line loop, layer ordering, residual scan
159	│   ├── config.py                  # YAML load + validation (paths/identifiers)
160	│   ├── subtable.py                # consistent substitution table
161	│   ├── rules/
162	│   │   ├── paths.py
163	│   │   ├── identifiers.py
164	│   │   ├── secrets.py             # vendored pattern library — the security floor
165	│   │   └── jitter.py              # v1 stub; design documented, not wired in
166	│   └── sidecar.py                 # redacted sidecar emission
167	├── tests/
168	│   ├── unit/
169	│   └── fixtures/                  # known-bad inputs (synthetic, pattern-matching)
170	└── README.md
171	```

174	
175	## 6b. Line-type stripping and traversal depth
176	
177	Two questions the line loop must answer explicitly. Both were under-specified in the first
178	draft and surfaced by architectural review (C-1, C-2); leaving them implicit would let two
179	implementers make incompatible — and unsafe — choices.
180	
181	### Step A — strip high-risk line types (before any transform)
182	
183	Some line types carry content that cannot be credibly pattern-scrubbed. **v0 drops them wholesale**
184	rather than ship a false sense of safety (see [D-7](#decision-d-7--v0-drops-high-risk-line-types)):
185	
186	- `file-history-snapshot` — `snapshot.trackedFileBackups` holds *entire pre-edit file contents*
187	  indexed by absolute path. Running path/identifier/secret regexes over arbitrary file bodies is
188	  not a credible scrub. v0 drops the line.
189	- `attachment` — image/binary payloads are opaque to regex.
190	
191	Stripping is governed by `--strip-types` (default: `file-history-snapshot,attachment`). Dropped
192	lines are counted in the sidecar (`stripped_lines:` block, [§10](#10-the-scrubbed-sidecar)).
193	
194	**Caveat for downstream analysis:** dropping `file-history-snapshot` means a sanitized fixture
195	cannot illustrate `/rewind` semantics. When a fixture needs that surface, build it
196	**synthetically** (the repo's default posture) rather than relaxing the strip list.
197	
198	### Step B — structural traversal, not stringify-and-regex
199	
200	Each surviving line is walked **structurally**: the parsed JSON object is traversed recursively
201	and rules are applied to every **string-valued leaf**, governed by an explicit **skip-list** of
202	fields left untouched:
203	
204	- **Skip-list (never scrubbed):** `message.model`, `version`, `type`, `*.role`, the numeric
205	  `usage.*` / `*_tokens` fields, `message.id` / `requestId` / `tool_use.id` / `tool_use_id` and
206	  the UUID fields (unless `remap_uuids` is on), and `thinking.signature` (replaced with a fixed
207	  placeholder, not scrubbed — see [§2](#2-background-what-makes-raw-session-jsonl-dangerous)).
208	- **Everything else that is a string leaf is scrubbed**, including the nested surfaces a
209	  line-level view hides: `message.content[].text`, `tool_use.input.*` (Bash `command`, Agent
210	  `prompt`, MCP inputs), `tool_result.content` (both string and array shapes),
211	  `toolUseResult.stdout`/`stderr`/`prompt`/`structuredPatch`, and every path-bearing field.
212	
213	Rationale (C-1): a structural walk with a skip-list makes the auditable question
214	*"which fields do we deliberately NOT scrub?"* — a short, reviewable list — instead of
215	*"did we remember to reach every field that might carry data?"*, which a stringify-and-regex
216	approach can never prove. Both `message.content` shapes fall out for free, because the walker
217	keys on string leaves, not on the line's shape. The residual secret scan ([§5](#5-design-principles--the-role-of-the-post-scrub-residual-scan))
218	still runs over the fully serialized output as the backstop, so a missed leaf is caught before
219	any file is written.
220	
221	---
222	
223	## 7. Layer 1: paths
224	
225	**What it does.** Replaces the home directory, the project slug, and configured absolute
226	paths with stable placeholders, consistently across the whole file.
227	
228	**Why paths run first.** Path normalization is the broadest structural transform. Running it
229	first means later layers see already-normalized text, and the residual scan at the end is the
230	backstop for any interaction effects.
231	
232	**Configuration** (YAML — see [§12 config model](#config-model-hybrid)):
233	
234	```yaml
235	paths:
236	  # ordered; first match wins. literal by default, or `re:` for regex.
237	  - match: "/home/user"
238	    replace: "/home/user"
239	  - match: "re:-home-user-([a-z0-9-]+)"   # project slug: scrub home, keep project name
240	    replace: "-home-user-\\1"
241	```
242	
243	**Consistency = determinism is the safety property.** Because replacements are deterministic
244	(no randomness), sanitizing the *parent* session and a *subagent trace* file in two separate
245	runs still yields a coherent set: `cwd` in the parent and `cwd` in the subagent both map to
246	`/home/user/...` identically. This is the reason v0 can safely operate one file at a time.
247	The moment a *randomized* transform is introduced (jitter, or UUID shuffling with a random
248	seed), per-file runs would diverge and a **session-bundle mode with a shared seed** becomes
249	necessary — which is one reason jitter is deferred (see [§9](#9-layer-4-jitter-deferred-to-v1-but-designed)).
250	
251	---
252	
253	## 8. Layer 2: identifiers
254	
255	**What it does.** Replaces configured emails, usernames, and (optionally) `gitBranch` values
256	with placeholders. Like paths, deterministic and consistent.
257	
258	```yaml
259	identifiers:
260	  - match: "user@example.com"
261	    replace: "user@example.com"
262	  - match: "re:[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}"   # catch-all email
263	    replace: "user@example.com"
264	options:
265	  scrub_git_branch: true      # gitBranch -> "feature/example" (branch names leak ticket IDs)
266	  remap_uuids: false          # see below
267	```
268	
269	**UUID remapping is off by default.** `uuid`/`parentUuid`/`sessionId`/`agentId` are
270	high-entropy random values that leak nothing on their own, so the default is to leave them.
271	When `remap_uuids: true`, the substitution table must remap them **consistently** so the
272	`parentUuid → uuid` graph, the `sessionId` shared key, and the `agentId` parent↔subagent link
273	all stay intact — a broken graph makes the fixture useless. Because consistent remapping with
274	a fixed seed is deterministic, it stays compatible with per-file runs; a *random* seed is what
275	forces bundle mode (see §7).
276	
277	---
278	
279	## 9. Layer 3: secrets
280	
281	**What it does.** Detects values matching known credential patterns and replaces each with a
282	**non-reversible** placeholder `<REDACTED:kind>` (e.g. `<REDACTED:anthropic-key>`). Secrets are
283	**redacted, never remapped** — there is no legitimate value to preserve.
284	
285	**The pattern library is code-defined, not YAML** (see [Decision D-1](#decision-d-1--rule-configuration-is-hybrid)),
286	and comes in two tiers in `rules/secrets.py`.
287	
288	**Tier 1 — vendored from the hook (sync-locked).** Copied verbatim from
289	[`.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py`](../../.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py):
290	
291	```python
292	VENDORED_PATTERNS = [               # MUST stay identical to the hook's SECRET_PATTERNS
293	    (r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}",     "anthropic-key"),
294	    (r"sk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}",    "openai-project-key"),
295	    (r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}",           "openai-key-legacy"),
296	    (r"ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}",          "github-pat-classic"),
297	    (r"github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{40,}",  "github-pat-fine"),
298	    (r"AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}",              "aws-access-key-id"),
299	    (r"AIza[A-Za-z0-9_-]{35}",         "gcp-api-key"),
300	]
301	```
302	
303	**Tier 2 — batch-only additions (sanitizer floor, C-3).** The hook fires on each *live tool
304	output*; the sanitizer scrubs a *whole session at rest*, which exposes credential shapes the
305	hook never had to catch — PEM private keys, bearer tokens, JWTs, and DB connection strings with
306	embedded passwords (all plausibly present in Bash `stdout` or a config file's contents). These
307	are **not** part of the sync-set:
308	
309	```python
310	BATCH_PATTERNS = [                  # sanitizer-only; NOT compared against the hook
311	    (r"-----BEGIN (?:RSA |EC |OPENSSH |DSA |PGP )?PRIVATE KEY-----", "pem-private-key"),
312	    (r"(?i)authorization:\s*bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]+",               "bearer-token"),
313	    (r"eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}", "jwt"),
314	    (r"(?i)(?:postgres(?:ql)?|mysql|mongodb(?:\+srv)?|redis|amqps?)://[^:\s/]+:[^@\s]+@", "conn-string-pw"),
315	    (r"xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}",                                "slack-token"),
316	]
317	SECRET_PATTERNS = VENDORED_PATTERNS + BATCH_PATTERNS
318	```
319	
320	**The sidecar never records the matched value** — not even truncated, since a prefix still
321	leaks entropy. Only `{matches: N}` per kind (see [§10](#10-the-scrubbed-sidecar)).
322	
323	**Config may *add* patterns, never remove built-ins.** The YAML accepts an additive
324	`extra_secret_patterns` list so a user can extend coverage (e.g. a company-internal token
325	shape). It cannot disable or weaken a built-in pattern — the floor is fixed in code.
326	
327	**Drift guard (I-4).** Vendoring duplicates Tier 1 between the hook and the sanitizer. The hook
328	stores **pre-compiled** `re.Pattern` objects while the sanitizer stores **raw strings**, so a
329	naive equality check fails. The sync-test (`tests/test_secret_patterns_in_sync.py`) normalizes
330	by extracting `.pattern` from each compiled hook regex, then compares the resulting
331	`(pattern_string, label)` tuples element-wise — order included — against `VENDORED_PATTERNS`.
332	`BATCH_PATTERNS` is explicitly excluded from the comparison. See
333	[Decision D-6](#decision-d-6--vendor-the-secret-pattern-library).
334	
335	### 9b. Layer 4: jitter (deferred to v1, but designed)
336	
337	**Decision D-3: jitter is not implemented in v0.** Rationale: it keeps the security-critical
338	core small and reviewable, and jitter is the one layer that introduces *randomness*, which
339	breaks the per-file determinism that makes v0's single-file model safe (see §7). It is the
340	natural first feature of v1, alongside session-bundle mode.
341	
342	**The v1 design, recorded now so the seam exists:**
343	
344	- **Granularity: per-session offset.** A single random offset (e.g. ±N days plus a
345	  within-day shift) is applied to *all* `timestamp` fields in a session, preserving the
346	  *relative* timing between lines (so durations, gaps, and cadence-of-thought remain
347	  analytically intact while the absolute wall-clock — which reveals working hours and dates
348	  — is destroyed). Per-field or per-message jitter was rejected: it would corrupt relative
349	  timing, which is exactly the analytically valuable signal, while adding configuration
350	  surface that is easy to get wrong.
351	- **Token-count jitter: off by default**, and when on, bounded (±small %) so accounting stays
352	  roughly faithful. Most sharing scenarios don't need it.
353	- **Shared seed → bundle mode.** Because jitter is randomized, a parent session and its
354	  subagent traces must be jittered with the **same seed and same offset** or their timestamps
355	  desynchronize. v1 therefore introduces a `--session-dir` mode that processes a parent plus
356	  its `subagents/*.jsonl` with one shared substitution table and one jitter seed.
357	
358	The `rules/jitter.py` module ships in v0 as a stub with this design in its docstring and a
359	`jitter: disabled` line in every v0 sidecar, so the format is forward-compatible.
360	
361	---
362	
363	## 10. The `.scrubbed` sidecar
364	
365	**Decision D-2: redacted per-substitution detail; secrets count-only; no original values.**
366	
367	The sidecar must be auditable (a reviewer can see *what kind* of thing changed and *how often*)
368	without itself becoming a leak surface. The README's original example embedded full
369	`original → replacement` mappings — that would store the very home dir and secrets you just
370	scrubbed, in a file sitting right next to the "safe" output. Rejected.
371	
372	Final format:
373	
374	```yaml
375	sanitizer_version: 0.1.0
376	scrubbed_at: 2026-05-29T18:30:00Z
377	input_filename: real-subagent-trace.jsonl       # basename only, never the full path
378	input_sha256: 9f2c...                            # one-way hash of the raw input (traceability)
379	config_version: 1
380	config_source: .ccs-sanitize.yaml
381	lines_processed: 512
382	stripped_lines:                                   # whole lines dropped (§6b, D-7)
383	  file-history-snapshot: 8
384	  attachment: 1
385	rules_applied:
386	  paths:       {substitutions: 14, distinct: 3}
387	  identifiers: {substitutions: 6,  distinct: 2}
388	  secrets:     {matches: 2}                       # redacted-and-removed; COUNT ONLY
389	  jitter:      disabled
390	substitutions:                                    # placeholders + replacement, never originals
391	  - {rule: paths,       placeholder: "<home-dir>",     replacement: "/home/user",          occurrences: 9}
392	  - {rule: paths,       placeholder: "<project-slug>", replacement: "-home-user-project",  occurrences: 5}
393	  - {rule: identifiers, placeholder: "<email>",        replacement: "user@example.com",    occurrences: 6}
394	residual_scan: clean                              # post-scrub secret re-scan result
395	```
396	
397	Notes:
398	
399	- `input_sha256` is a one-way hash of the *raw* input — it aids traceability and dedup and is
400	  safe (not reversible). It resolves the README's ambiguous "input_hash ... not stored" note:
401	  the raw input is not stored; its hash is.
402	- The `substitutions` block shows the *replacement* and a generic `placeholder` category, but
403	  **never the original**. **Replacements must themselves be non-sensitive (I-3):** the sidecar
404	  reproduces them verbatim, so a config that maps a path to another real path would leak through
405	  the sidecar. Config validation rejects a replacement that itself matches any path/identifier/
406	  secret rule, and the docs steer users to generic targets (`/home/user`, `user@example.com`).
407	- `stripped_lines` records whole lines dropped by `--strip-types` ([§6b](#6b-line-type-stripping-and-traversal-depth));
408	  their contents are never inspected or surfaced.
409	- Secrets contribute only a count. No matched bytes, no kind-level original, nothing reversible.
410	- `residual_scan: clean` is always present and always `clean` on a written file — if it were
411	  not clean, the file would not have been written.
412

414	
415	## 11. CLI shape & fail-closed behavior
416	
417	```
418	ccs-sanitize <input.jsonl> -o <output.jsonl> [options]
419	
420	Options:
421	  -o, --output PATH       Output JSONL path (required). Sidecar is <output>.scrubbed.
422	  -c, --config PATH       Rules YAML. Default: ./.ccs-sanitize.yaml or alongside input.
423	      --dry-run           Scan and print the sidecar to stdout; write nothing.
424	      --force             Allow overwriting an existing output file (default: refuse).
425	      --strip-types LIST  Line types dropped wholesale (§6b). Default:
426	                          file-history-snapshot,attachment.
427	  -v, --verbose           Per-rule progress to stderr.
428	      --version           Print sanitizer version.
429	```
430	
431	**Exit codes (fail-closed):**
432	
433	| Code | Meaning | Output written? |
434	|---|---|---|
435	| 0 | Success | yes (+ sidecar) |
436	| 1 | Usage error (bad args, missing input, output exists without `--force`) | no |
437	| 2 | **Safety failure** — rule raised, line failed to parse, or residual scan found a secret | **no** |
438	| 3 | Config error (YAML invalid, regex won't compile, attempt to disable a built-in pattern) | no |
439	
440	**Atomicity & rename order (I-5).** Output and sidecar are written to temp files in the
441	destination directory and renamed into place only after the full file is processed *and* the
442	residual scan passes. The **sidecar is renamed first, then the output** — so a crash in the
443	gap can leave an orphan sidecar (harmless, and overwritten on re-run) but can never leave a
444	scrubbed output with no sidecar, which would otherwise pass a sidecar-existence check while
445	being unaccounted for. A failed or interrupted run never leaves a partial scrub.
446	
447	**Serialization is pinned for determinism (I-1).** Output lines are re-emitted with
448	`json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))` and **original key order preserved**
449	(Python's `json.loads` keeps insertion order, so a straight round-trip is
450	order-stable; keys are *not* sorted). Pinning these parameters is what turns "deterministic
451	output" from a claim into a property — without it, two environments could emit byte-different
452	but semantically equal output and break the determinism and idempotency tests.
453	
454	**Malformed JSONL aborts (no skip flag in v0).** A session file should be well-formed; a parse
455	error means something is wrong, so the safe action is to stop. No `--skip-malformed` escape
456	hatch ships in v0 — adding a way to silently drop lines is a footgun on a security tool.
457	
458	**The CLI is the sanctioned reader of raw sessions.** The [`block_secret_reads.py`](../../.claude/hooks/block_secret_reads.py)
459	hook blocks `Read`/`Edit`/`Grep`/`Glob` on `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` but deliberately
460	**not Bash** — so `ccs-sanitize ~/.claude/projects/.../sess.jsonl -o fixtures/sanitized/...`,
461	invoked via Bash, is the intended path for turning a raw session into a committable fixture.
462	
463	---
464	
465	## 12. Packaging & configuration
466	
467	### Packaging — in-repo only for v0
468	
469	**Decision D-5: in-repo only for v0; not published to PyPI.** Per the roadmap. A `pyproject.toml`
470	with a `ccs-sanitize` entry point lives at `tooling/sanitizer/`, uv-managed. Dependencies are
471	kept minimal: stdlib for the pipeline and secret patterns (mirroring the hooks' stdlib-only
472	constraint), plus PyYAML for config parsing. Target Python 3.11+. Extraction to a standalone
473	PyPI package (`claude-code-sessions-sanitizer`) is deferred until a standalone audience
474	materializes — the module layout is kept import-clean so extraction is mechanical later.
475	
476	### Config model — hybrid {#config-model-hybrid}
477	
478	**Decision D-1: hybrid.** Secret patterns are **code-defined** (the non-weakenable security
479	floor); path and identifier rules are **YAML-configured per project** (`.ccs-sanitize.yaml`).
480	YAML may *add* secret patterns (`extra_secret_patterns`) but never remove built-ins.
481	
482	Rationale: a security tool whose secret detection can be silently weakened by editing a config
483	file is a tool that will eventually be weakened by a careless edit. Keeping the floor in code
484	means the worst a bad config can do is over-scrub (safe) or fail to add a project-specific
485	path rule (visible in the sidecar counts), never under-detect a secret.
486	
487	Full config schema:
488	
489	```yaml
490	version: 1
491	paths:        [ {match: "...", replace: "..."}, ... ]   # ordered, first-match-wins
492	identifiers:  [ {match: "...", replace: "..."}, ... ]
493	options:
494	  scrub_git_branch: true
495	  remap_uuids: false
496	extra_secret_patterns:                                   # ADDITIVE only
497	  - {pattern: "re:CORP-[A-Z0-9]{32}", kind: "corp-token"}
498	```
499	
500	---
501	
502	## 13. Fixture-validator integration
503	
504	**Decision D-4: the validator re-scans independently and never trusts the sidecar.**
505	
506	When [`tooling/fixture-validator/`](../../tooling/fixture-validator/README.md) checks a file
507	in `fixtures/sanitized/`, it:
508	
509	1. Confirms a `.scrubbed` sidecar exists and its `sanitizer_version` is recognized.
510	2. **Independently re-runs the secret-pattern scan** over the fixture contents.
511	3. Optionally verifies `input_sha256` shape and required sidecar keys.
512	
513	The validator does *not* trust the sidecar's `residual_scan: clean` as proof — it re-derives
514	it. This is defense in depth: a stale sidecar (output edited after scrub), a forged sidecar, or
515	a sanitizer bug all get caught at the validator layer. The cost is a cheap second regex pass;
516	the benefit is that fixture safety does not depend on the sanitizer having been bug-free at
517	scrub time. The "hybrid / trust counts" option was rejected — re-scanning is cheap enough that
518	there's no reason to trust *any* part of the security claim.
519	
520	---
521	
522	## 14. Testing strategy
523	
524	Known-bad inputs live in `tests/fixtures/`. **They are synthetic and contain pattern-matching-but-fake secrets**
525	(e.g. `sk-ant-` followed by 25 `A`s) — never a real key.
526	This is itself a security requirement: the test suite must not be the thing that commits a
527	real credential.
528	
529	Coverage:
530	
531	- **Per-surface scrub tests** — a fixture line carrying each: home dir, project slug, absolute
532	  path, email, git branch with a ticket ID, and each Tier-1 and Tier-2 secret pattern. Assert
533	  the output contains none of the original tokens and the sidecar counts are correct.
534	- **Structural-traversal test (C-1)** — secrets/paths planted in *nested* leaves the line-level
535	  view hides (`tool_use.input.command`, `toolUseResult.stdout`, `tool_result.content` array
536	  shape, `message.content[].text`); assert all are scrubbed and skip-list fields
537	  (`message.model`, `usage.*`, `thinking.signature`) are untouched.
538	- **Strip-types test (C-2/D-7)** — input with `file-history-snapshot` and `attachment` lines;
539	  assert they are dropped, counted in `stripped_lines`, and no `trackedFileBackups` content
540	  survives anywhere in the output.
541	- **Residual-scan / fail-closed test** — craft an input where naive redaction could be bypassed
542	  (a secret split across a transform boundary); assert the residual scan catches it, the run
543	  exits 2, and no output file exists.
544	- **No-partial-scrub test** — induce a rule error mid-file; assert no output and no sidecar.
545	- **Determinism test** — same input + config → byte-identical output across two runs (pins the
546	  serialization parameters from [§11](#11-cli-shape--fail-closed-behavior)).
547	- **Idempotency test** — sanitizing an already-sanitized file is a no-op (0 substitutions,
548	  `residual_scan: clean`).
549	- **Sidecar-never-leaks test** — assert no original sensitive token (home dir, email, secret)
550	  *and no configured replacement that is itself sensitive* appears anywhere in the sidecar (I-3).
551	- **Pattern-sync test** (repo-level) — normalize the hook's compiled `SECRET_PATTERNS` via
552	  `.pattern` and assert element-wise equality with `VENDORED_PATTERNS` (drift guard from §9);
553	  `BATCH_PATTERNS` excluded.
554	
555	---
556	
557	## 15. Open questions — resolutions
558	
559	Every open question from [`tooling/sanitizer/README.md`](../../tooling/sanitizer/README.md)
560	and the [epic](https://github.com/real-user/claude-code-sessions/issues/1),
561	with its resolution. All resolved 2026-05-29.
562	
563	| # | Source | Question | Resolution | Decision |
564	|---|---|---|---|---|
565	| 1 | README | YAML-configured vs code-defined rules | **Hybrid** — secrets in code (additive-only YAML extension), paths/identifiers in YAML | [D-1](#decision-d-1--rule-configuration-is-hybrid) |
566	| 2 | README | Sidecar: substitution dictionaries vs counts | **Redacted per-substitution detail**; secrets count-only; no original values | [D-2](#decision-d-2--redacted-sidecar) |
567	| 3 | README | Jitter granularity (field/message/session) | **Deferred to v1**; designed as per-session offset | [D-3](#9b-layer-4-jitter-deferred-to-v1-but-designed) |
568	| 4 | README | Validator: re-scan vs trust sidecar | **Independent re-scan**, never trust the sidecar | [D-4](#13-fixture-validator-integration) |
569	| 5 | Roadmap | PyPI package vs in-repo | **In-repo only for v0** | [D-5](#packaging--in-repo-only-for-v0) |
570	| 6 | Roadmap | Secret-pattern library: copy vs dependency | **Vendor (copy)** into the sanitizer; sync-test guards drift | [D-6](#decision-d-6--vendor-the-secret-pattern-library) |
571	| 7 | Review | High-risk line types (`file-history-snapshot`, `attachment`) | **Dropped wholesale in v0** via `--strip-types`; synthetic fixtures cover those surfaces | [D-7](#decision-d-7--v0-drops-high-risk-line-types) |
572	
573	### Decision D-1 — rule configuration is hybrid
574	Secrets code-defined (non-weakenable floor, additive YAML extension allowed); paths/identifiers
575	in YAML. A config-weakenable security floor will eventually be weakened by accident; keeping it
576	in code means a bad config can only over-scrub or miss a path rule, never under-detect a secret.
577	
578	### Decision D-2 — redacted sidecar
579	Per-substitution detail using category placeholders and the (non-sensitive) replacement value;
580	secrets contribute a count only; no original values anywhere. Keeps the sidecar auditable
581	without making it a second copy of the data we just scrubbed.
582	
583	### Decision D-6 — vendor the secret-pattern library
584	This repo is **upstream** of AgentFluent (per [CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) and the data
585	dictionary). Taking a runtime dependency on AgentFluent would invert that relationship. The
586	pattern set is therefore copied into `rules/secrets.py`, which becomes a candidate canonical
587	home; a future task can have the hook and/or AgentFluent consume from here. A repo-level
588	sync-test prevents the vendored Tier-1 copy and the hook's copy from drifting in the meantime.
589	
590	### Decision D-7 — v0 drops high-risk line types
591	`file-history-snapshot` (full file contents in `trackedFileBackups`) and `attachment` (opaque
592	binary/image payloads) cannot be credibly scrubbed with pattern rules. v0 drops them wholesale
593	(`--strip-types`, counted in the sidecar) rather than ship a false sense of safety. Surfaces
594	that need those line types in a fixture are built synthetically. Content-level scrubbing is
595	future work ([§17](#17-future-work-v1)). Surfaced by architect review (C-2), 2026-05-29.
596	
597	---
598	
599	## 16. Phasing & acceptance criteria
600	
601	**Phase 1 (this document):** PRD accepted. Done when every open question in §15 is resolved
602	and the design is signed off.
603	
604	**Phase 2 (implementation):** acceptance criteria from the [epic](https://github.com/real-user/claude-code-sessions/issues/1):
605	
606	- [ ] CLI usable as `ccs-sanitize <input.jsonl> -o <output.jsonl>`
607	- [ ] Strip-types step drops `file-history-snapshot`/`attachment` (§6b); structural traversal
608	      with skip-list reaches nested leaves (§6b)
609	- [ ] Layered rules: paths → identifiers → secrets (jitter stub present, disabled)
610	- [ ] `.scrubbed` sidecar in the redacted format of §10
611	- [ ] Fails closed: any rule error or residual secret aborts; no partial scrubs
612	- [ ] Test suite covers the known-bad inputs of §14
613	- [ ] At least one real session sanitized and committed to `fixtures/sanitized/` with sidecar
614	
615	---
616	
617	## 17. Future work (v1+)
618	
619	- **Jitter** (per-session offset) + **session-bundle mode** (`--session-dir`, shared seed) —
620	  the two are coupled (§9b).
621	- **PyPI extraction** as `claude-code-sessions-sanitizer` if a standalone audience appears.
622	- **Interactive review mode** — surface free-text prompts/outputs for human confirmation,
623	  addressing the §4 free-text limitation.
624	- **Content-level handling of `file-history-snapshot`** — scrub `trackedFileBackups` file
625	  bodies (path-aware, per-file-type) instead of dropping the line wholesale (D-7), so sanitized
626	  fixtures can illustrate `/rewind` semantics.
627	- **Shared secret-pattern source** — collapse the vendored Tier-1 duplication (§9) once the
628	  canonical home is decided.
629	
630	---
631	
632	## 18. Decision history
633	
634	| Date | Change |
635	|---|---|
636	| 2026-05-29 | PRD created. D-1 through D-6 decided (§15). Jitter deferred to v1. |
637	| 2026-05-29 | Architect review incorporated ([issue #1 comment](https://github.com/real-user/claude-code-sessions/issues/1)): structural-traversal + strip-types spec (§6b, C-1/C-2), D-7 added, secret floor expanded to two tiers (§9, C-3), serialization pinned + rename order (§11, I-1/I-5), replacement-leak guard (§10, I-3), sync-test comparison shape (§9, I-4). |
638

# PRD — Session JSONL Sanitizer (`ccs-sanitize`)

**Status:** Design (Phase 1 of W2). Implementation has not started.
**Owner:** Real Name
**Roadmap item:** [W2 — Sanitizer design + v0 implementation](roadmap-v0.md#w2--sanitizer-design--v0-implementation)
**Tracking issue:** [#1 — Epic: Sanitizer design + v0 implementation](https://github.com/real-user/claude-code-sessions/issues/1)
**Created:** 2026-05-29
**Last updated:** 2026-05-29

> This PRD is deliberately verbose. Per the epic, we are early-stage and want the
> design rationale, the alternatives considered, and the decision history recorded
> alongside the final spec — not just the spec. Sections marked **Decision** record a
> resolved question; sections marked **Alternatives** record what was rejected and why.

---

## 1. Purpose

`ccs-sanitize` is the CLI tool that scrubs raw Claude Code session JSONL files so they
can be committed to this repository (as `fixtures/sanitized/`) or shared publicly by
anyone. It is the **security boundary** of the whole project: without it, every fixture
must be synthetic, which limits which real-world phenomena the blog can illustrate
(a multi-hour real subagent trace, real token-accounting shapes, real tool-error cascades).

The tool has two audiences:

1. **This repo.** Produces the `.scrubbed` sidecar that gates `fixtures/sanitized/`
   (see [CLAUDE.md → Security posture](../../CLAUDE.md) and
   [fixtures conventions](../../CLAUDE.md)).
2. **Standalone users.** Anyone who wants to share a Claude Code session — in a bug
   report, a blog post, a gist — without leaking secrets, file paths, or personal
   identifiers. "Sanitize your Claude Code session before sharing" is a real, unmet need,
   and the tool is designed to stand on its own (see [§12 Packaging](#12-packaging)).

---

## 2. Background: what makes raw session JSONL dangerous

The [data dictionary](../../reference/data-dictionary.md) documents the format in full.
For sanitization purposes, the dangerous surfaces are:

| Surface | Where it lives | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| **Home directory & username** | `cwd`, `toolUseResult.file`/`filePath`, the project slug (`-home-USER-project`), `transcript_path` echoes | Leaks the OS username and directory layout on every line. |
| **Absolute file paths** | `cwd`, tool inputs (`file_path`, `command`), `toolUseResult` path fields, `structuredPatch` | Leaks project structure, internal names, sometimes employer/client identity. |
| **Project slug** | the directory name *and* `cwd` on every line | Encodes home dir + project path together; must be scrubbed consistently with `cwd`. |
| **Identifiers** | git author email, `gitBranch` (often `feature/JIRA-123-...`), prompt text | PII and internal ticket/project names. |
| **Secrets** | Bash `stdout`/`stderr`, file contents via `Read`, env dumps, prompt text | API keys, tokens — the catastrophic case. Patterns in [`.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py`](../../.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py). |
| **Whole-file backups** | `file-history-snapshot.snapshot.trackedFileBackups` — full pre-edit file contents indexed by absolute path | **Highest-risk field in the format.** Holds entire files (configs, source, possibly `.env` snapshots). v0 **drops these lines wholesale** rather than scrub arbitrary contents — see [§6b](#6b-line-type-stripping-and-traversal-depth) and [D-7](#decision-d-7--v0-drops-high-risk-line-types). |
| **Tool inputs** | `tool_use.input` — Bash `command`, Agent `prompt`, MCP tool inputs (arbitrary schemas) | Commands and prompts carry paths, secrets, and free-text PII. Reached only via structural traversal ([§6b](#6b-line-type-stripping-and-traversal-depth)). |
| **Subagent / free-text prompts** | `toolUseResult.prompt`, `SubagentStart.initial_prompt` | Concentrated free-text PII — the full prompt handed to a subagent. |
| **Free-text prompts & tool output** | `message.content` (string and array shapes), `tool_result.content` | Arbitrary content. May contain names, company info, proprietary code. **Not reliably auto-scrubbable** — see [§4 Non-goals](#4-non-goals). |
| **Attachments** | `attachment` lines; image content blocks | Opaque to regex (binary/base64). v0 **drops `attachment` lines** — see [D-7](#decision-d-7--v0-drops-high-risk-line-types). |
| **Thinking signatures** | `thinking.signature` | High-entropy opaque blob; can false-positive on secret patterns. Replaced with a fixed placeholder (no analytical value in a fixture). |
| **Timestamps** | `timestamp` on most lines | Reveals working hours, session duration, cadence — a fingerprint. Addressed by jitter ([§9](#9-layer-4-jitter-deferred-to-v1-but-designed)), deferred to v1. |
| **UUIDs** | `uuid`, `parentUuid`, `sessionId`, `agentId`, `requestId`, `message.id`, `tool_use.id` | Not inherently sensitive (high-entropy random), but if remapped the conversation graph must stay linked. Remapping is **off by default** ([§8](#8-layer-2-identifiers)). |

Two surfaces are **out of scope by design**: model IDs/versions (`message.model`, `version`)
and token-accounting numbers (`usage.*`) carry no PII and are analytically valuable, so the
sanitizer leaves them untouched (token counts are only perturbed by the deferred jitter layer,
and even then off by default).

---

## 3. Goals

- **Fail-closed.** Any rule error, any malformed line, or any secret surviving to the
  output aborts the run with a non-zero exit and **no output file**. There is never a
  partial scrub.
- **No silent transforms.** The `.scrubbed` sidecar enumerates every category of change so
  a human reviewer can audit what happened — without the sidecar itself becoming a leak.
- **Deterministic.** Same input + same config → byte-identical output. This is what makes
  per-file runs safe (see [§7 consistency](#consistency-determinism-is-the-safety-property))
  and keeps committed fixtures git-stable.
- **Layered.** Independent rule layers (paths → identifiers → secrets → jitter) applied in a
  fixed order, each independently testable.
- **Versioned output.** Every sidecar records `sanitizer_version`; downstream consumers
  (the fixture-validator, sibling projects) can trust or distrust by version.
- **Standalone.** Usable with no dependency on this repo's layout or on AgentFluent/CodeFluent.

---

## 4. Non-goals

These are **explicitly out of scope** and the PRD states them loudly because over-trusting
the sanitizer is the most likely way to leak data.

- **The sanitizer is not a guarantee against all PII in free-text prompts.** It catches
  *structured* leaks — paths, configured identifiers, and secret *patterns*. It cannot catch
  "my name is Jane and I work at AcmeCorp" typed into a prompt. Mitigations: the sidecar
  drives human review, and the repo's standing policy keeps **synthetic the default**
  (per [CLAUDE.md fixtures](../../CLAUDE.md) — use sanitized "only when realistic data shape
  can't be reproduced synthetically").
- **No GUI / interactive review mode** (deferred; see [§14](#14-future-work-v1)).
- **No streaming sanitization of live sessions.** Operates on files at rest.
- **No automatic upload** to any destination. The tool writes local files; publishing is a
  separate, human-initiated step.
- **No reverse-mapping.** The scrub is one-way. The sidecar deliberately cannot reconstruct
  the original (see [§10](#10-the-scrubbed-sidecar)).
- **Jitter is designed but not implemented in v0** (see [§9](#9-layer-4-jitter-deferred-to-v1-but-designed)).

---

## 5. Design principles & the role of the post-scrub residual scan

The single most important safety mechanism is the **residual secret scan**: after all
transform layers have run, the sanitizer re-runs the secret-pattern detector over the
*output*. If anything matches, a secret survived redaction (a bug, or a secret split across
a transform boundary, or an unknown encoding) — the run **aborts and writes nothing**.

This means the design has two distinct secret interactions, and conflating them is a common
mistake:

1. **Detection during scrub** (expected): secret patterns match in the input → redacted →
   counted in the sidecar. A secret match here is normal — it's the tool doing its job.
2. **Residual verification after scrub** (must be clean): the same patterns run over the
   output. A match here is a failure condition, not a normal event.

The residual scan is also why the fixture-validator re-scans independently rather than
trusting the sidecar (see [§11](#11-fixture-validator-integration)) — defense in depth, the
same check enforced at two layers owned by two tools.

---

## 6. Architecture overview

A line-oriented pipeline. Each JSONL line is parsed, passed through the ordered transform
layers, and re-serialized. The substitution table accumulates across lines so replacements
are **consistent within a file** (the same real home dir maps to the same placeholder on
line 1 and line 5,000).

```
input.jsonl
   │
   ▼  parse line (fail-closed on malformed JSON)
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Layer 1: paths        (deterministic remap) │
│  Layer 2: identifiers  (deterministic remap) │
│  Layer 3: secrets      (redact + count)      │
│  Layer 4: jitter       (DEFERRED to v1)      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   │  accumulate substitution table + counts
   ▼  (all lines processed)
residual secret scan over full output  ──► match? ABORT, no output
   │  clean
   ▼
atomic write: output.jsonl  +  output.jsonl.scrubbed
```

Module layout (matches the [README's planned shape](../../tooling/sanitizer/README.md)):

```
tooling/sanitizer/
├── pyproject.toml                 # uv-managed; entry point `ccs-sanitize`
├── src/ccs_sanitize/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── cli.py                     # arg parsing, exit codes, atomic write
│   ├── pipeline.py                # line loop, layer ordering, residual scan
│   ├── config.py                  # YAML load + validation (paths/identifiers)
│   ├── subtable.py                # consistent substitution table
│   ├── rules/
│   │   ├── paths.py
│   │   ├── identifiers.py
│   │   ├── secrets.py             # vendored pattern library — the security floor
│   │   └── jitter.py              # v1 stub; design documented, not wired in
│   └── sidecar.py                 # redacted sidecar emission
├── tests/
│   ├── unit/
│   └── fixtures/                  # known-bad inputs (synthetic, pattern-matching)
└── README.md
```

---

## 6b. Line-type stripping and traversal depth

Two questions the line loop must answer explicitly. Both were under-specified in the first
draft and surfaced by architectural review (C-1, C-2); leaving them implicit would let two
implementers make incompatible — and unsafe — choices.

### Step A — strip high-risk line types (before any transform)

Some line types carry content that cannot be credibly pattern-scrubbed. **v0 drops them wholesale**
rather than ship a false sense of safety (see [D-7](#decision-d-7--v0-drops-high-risk-line-types)):

- `file-history-snapshot` — `snapshot.trackedFileBackups` holds *entire pre-edit file contents*
  indexed by absolute path. Running path/identifier/secret regexes over arbitrary file bodies is
  not a credible scrub. v0 drops the line.
- `attachment` — image/binary payloads are opaque to regex.

Stripping is governed by `--strip-types` (default: `file-history-snapshot,attachment`). Dropped
lines are counted in the sidecar (`stripped_lines:` block, [§10](#10-the-scrubbed-sidecar)).

**Caveat for downstream analysis:** dropping `file-history-snapshot` means a sanitized fixture
cannot illustrate `/rewind` semantics. When a fixture needs that surface, build it
**synthetically** (the repo's default posture) rather than relaxing the strip list.

### Step B — structural traversal, not stringify-and-regex

Each surviving line is walked **structurally**: the parsed JSON object is traversed recursively
and rules are applied to every **string-valued leaf**, governed by an explicit **skip-list** of
fields left untouched:

- **Skip-list (never scrubbed):** `message.model`, `version`, `type`, `*.role`, the numeric
  `usage.*` / `*_tokens` fields, `message.id` / `requestId` / `tool_use.id` / `tool_use_id` and
  the UUID fields (unless `remap_uuids` is on), and `thinking.signature` (replaced with a fixed
  placeholder, not scrubbed — see [§2](#2-background-what-makes-raw-session-jsonl-dangerous)).
- **Everything else that is a string leaf is scrubbed**, including the nested surfaces a
  line-level view hides: `message.content[].text`, `tool_use.input.*` (Bash `command`, Agent
  `prompt`, MCP inputs), `tool_result.content` (both string and array shapes),
  `toolUseResult.stdout`/`stderr`/`prompt`/`structuredPatch`, and every path-bearing field.

Rationale (C-1): a structural walk with a skip-list makes the auditable question
*"which fields do we deliberately NOT scrub?"* — a short, reviewable list — instead of
*"did we remember to reach every field that might carry data?"*, which a stringify-and-regex
approach can never prove. Both `message.content` shapes fall out for free, because the walker
keys on string leaves, not on the line's shape. The residual secret scan ([§5](#5-design-principles--the-role-of-the-post-scrub-residual-scan))
still runs over the fully serialized output as the backstop, so a missed leaf is caught before
any file is written.

---

## 7. Layer 1: paths

**What it does.** Replaces the home directory, the project slug, and configured absolute
paths with stable placeholders, consistently across the whole file.

**Why paths run first.** Path normalization is the broadest structural transform. Running it
first means later layers see already-normalized text, and the residual scan at the end is the
backstop for any interaction effects.

**Configuration** (YAML — see [§12 config model](#config-model-hybrid)):

```yaml
paths:
  # ordered; first match wins. literal by default, or `re:` for regex.
  - match: "/home/user"
    replace: "/home/user"
  - match: "re:-home-user-([a-z0-9-]+)"   # project slug: scrub home, keep project name
    replace: "-home-user-\\1"
```

**Consistency = determinism is the safety property.** Because replacements are deterministic
(no randomness), sanitizing the *parent* session and a *subagent trace* file in two separate
runs still yields a coherent set: `cwd` in the parent and `cwd` in the subagent both map to
`/home/user/...` identically. This is the reason v0 can safely operate one file at a time.
The moment a *randomized* transform is introduced (jitter, or UUID shuffling with a random
seed), per-file runs would diverge and a **session-bundle mode with a shared seed** becomes
necessary — which is one reason jitter is deferred (see [§9](#9-layer-4-jitter-deferred-to-v1-but-designed)).

---

## 8. Layer 2: identifiers

**What it does.** Replaces configured emails, usernames, and (optionally) `gitBranch` values
with placeholders. Like paths, deterministic and consistent.

```yaml
identifiers:
  - match: "user@example.com"
    replace: "user@example.com"
  - match: "re:[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}"   # catch-all email
    replace: "user@example.com"
options:
  scrub_git_branch: true      # gitBranch -> "feature/example" (branch names leak ticket IDs)
  remap_uuids: false          # see below
```

**UUID remapping is off by default.** `uuid`/`parentUuid`/`sessionId`/`agentId` are
high-entropy random values that leak nothing on their own, so the default is to leave them.
When `remap_uuids: true`, the substitution table must remap them **consistently** so the
`parentUuid → uuid` graph, the `sessionId` shared key, and the `agentId` parent↔subagent link
all stay intact — a broken graph makes the fixture useless. Because consistent remapping with
a fixed seed is deterministic, it stays compatible with per-file runs; a *random* seed is what
forces bundle mode (see §7).

---

## 9. Layer 3: secrets

**What it does.** Detects values matching known credential patterns and replaces each with a
**non-reversible** placeholder `<REDACTED:kind>` (e.g. `<REDACTED:anthropic-key>`). Secrets are
**redacted, never remapped** — there is no legitimate value to preserve.

**The pattern library is code-defined, not YAML** (see [Decision D-1](#decision-d-1--rule-configuration-is-hybrid)),
and comes in two tiers in `rules/secrets.py`.

**Tier 1 — vendored from the hook (sync-locked).** Copied verbatim from
[`.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py`](../../.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py):

```python
VENDORED_PATTERNS = [               # MUST stay identical to the hook's SECRET_PATTERNS
    (r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}",     "anthropic-key"),
    (r"sk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}",    "openai-project-key"),
    (r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}",           "openai-key-legacy"),
    (r"ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}",          "github-pat-classic"),
    (r"github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{40,}",  "github-pat-fine"),
    (r"AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}",              "aws-access-key-id"),
    (r"AIza[A-Za-z0-9_-]{35}",         "gcp-api-key"),
]
```

**Tier 2 — batch-only additions (sanitizer floor, C-3).** The hook fires on each *live tool
output*; the sanitizer scrubs a *whole session at rest*, which exposes credential shapes the
hook never had to catch — PEM private keys, bearer tokens, JWTs, and DB connection strings with
embedded passwords (all plausibly present in Bash `stdout` or a config file's contents). These
are **not** part of the sync-set:

```python
BATCH_PATTERNS = [                  # sanitizer-only; NOT compared against the hook
    (r"-----BEGIN (?:RSA |EC |OPENSSH |DSA |PGP )?PRIVATE KEY-----", "pem-private-key"),
    (r"(?i)authorization:\s*bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]+",               "bearer-token"),
    (r"eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}", "jwt"),
    (r"(?i)(?:postgres(?:ql)?|mysql|mongodb(?:\+srv)?|redis|amqps?)://[^:\s/]+:[^@\s]+@", "conn-string-pw"),
    (r"xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}",                                "slack-token"),
]
SECRET_PATTERNS = VENDORED_PATTERNS + BATCH_PATTERNS
```

**The sidecar never records the matched value** — not even truncated, since a prefix still
leaks entropy. Only `{matches: N}` per kind (see [§10](#10-the-scrubbed-sidecar)).

**Config may *add* patterns, never remove built-ins.** The YAML accepts an additive
`extra_secret_patterns` list so a user can extend coverage (e.g. a company-internal token
shape). It cannot disable or weaken a built-in pattern — the floor is fixed in code.

**Drift guard (I-4).** Vendoring duplicates Tier 1 between the hook and the sanitizer. The hook
stores **pre-compiled** `re.Pattern` objects while the sanitizer stores **raw strings**, so a
naive equality check fails. The sync-test (`tests/test_secret_patterns_in_sync.py`) normalizes
by extracting `.pattern` from each compiled hook regex, then compares the resulting
`(pattern_string, label)` tuples element-wise — order included — against `VENDORED_PATTERNS`.
`BATCH_PATTERNS` is explicitly excluded from the comparison. See
[Decision D-6](#decision-d-6--vendor-the-secret-pattern-library).

### 9b. Layer 4: jitter (deferred to v1, but designed)

**Decision D-3: jitter is not implemented in v0.** Rationale: it keeps the security-critical
core small and reviewable, and jitter is the one layer that introduces *randomness*, which
breaks the per-file determinism that makes v0's single-file model safe (see §7). It is the
natural first feature of v1, alongside session-bundle mode.

**The v1 design, recorded now so the seam exists:**

- **Granularity: per-session offset.** A single random offset (e.g. ±N days plus a
  within-day shift) is applied to *all* `timestamp` fields in a session, preserving the
  *relative* timing between lines (so durations, gaps, and cadence-of-thought remain
  analytically intact while the absolute wall-clock — which reveals working hours and dates
  — is destroyed). Per-field or per-message jitter was rejected: it would corrupt relative
  timing, which is exactly the analytically valuable signal, while adding configuration
  surface that is easy to get wrong.
- **Token-count jitter: off by default**, and when on, bounded (±small %) so accounting stays
  roughly faithful. Most sharing scenarios don't need it.
- **Shared seed → bundle mode.** Because jitter is randomized, a parent session and its
  subagent traces must be jittered with the **same seed and same offset** or their timestamps
  desynchronize. v1 therefore introduces a `--session-dir` mode that processes a parent plus
  its `subagents/*.jsonl` with one shared substitution table and one jitter seed.

The `rules/jitter.py` module ships in v0 as a stub with this design in its docstring and a
`jitter: disabled` line in every v0 sidecar, so the format is forward-compatible.

---

## 10. The `.scrubbed` sidecar

**Decision D-2: redacted per-substitution detail; secrets count-only; no original values.**

The sidecar must be auditable (a reviewer can see *what kind* of thing changed and *how often*)
without itself becoming a leak surface. The README's original example embedded full
`original → replacement` mappings — that would store the very home dir and secrets you just
scrubbed, in a file sitting right next to the "safe" output. Rejected.

Final format:

```yaml
sanitizer_version: 0.1.0
scrubbed_at: 2026-05-29T18:30:00Z
input_filename: real-subagent-trace.jsonl       # basename only, never the full path
input_sha256: 9f2c...                            # one-way hash of the raw input (traceability)
config_version: 1
config_source: .ccs-sanitize.yaml
lines_processed: 512
stripped_lines:                                   # whole lines dropped (§6b, D-7)
  file-history-snapshot: 8
  attachment: 1
rules_applied:
  paths:       {substitutions: 14, distinct: 3}
  identifiers: {substitutions: 6,  distinct: 2}
  secrets:     {matches: 2}                       # redacted-and-removed; COUNT ONLY
  jitter:      disabled
substitutions:                                    # placeholders + replacement, never originals
  - {rule: paths,       placeholder: "<home-dir>",     replacement: "/home/user",          occurrences: 9}
  - {rule: paths,       placeholder: "<project-slug>", replacement: "-home-user-project",  occurrences: 5}
  - {rule: identifiers, placeholder: "<email>",        replacement: "user@example.com",    occurrences: 6}
residual_scan: clean                              # post-scrub secret re-scan result
```

Notes:

- `input_sha256` is a one-way hash of the *raw* input — it aids traceability and dedup and is
  safe (not reversible). It resolves the README's ambiguous "input_hash ... not stored" note:
  the raw input is not stored; its hash is.
- The `substitutions` block shows the *replacement* and a generic `placeholder` category, but
  **never the original**. **Replacements must themselves be non-sensitive (I-3):** the sidecar
  reproduces them verbatim, so a config that maps a path to another real path would leak through
  the sidecar. Config validation rejects a replacement that itself matches any path/identifier/
  secret rule, and the docs steer users to generic targets (`/home/user`, `user@example.com`).
- `stripped_lines` records whole lines dropped by `--strip-types` ([§6b](#6b-line-type-stripping-and-traversal-depth));
  their contents are never inspected or surfaced.
- Secrets contribute only a count. No matched bytes, no kind-level original, nothing reversible.
- `residual_scan: clean` is always present and always `clean` on a written file — if it were
  not clean, the file would not have been written.

---

## 11. CLI shape & fail-closed behavior

```
ccs-sanitize <input.jsonl> -o <output.jsonl> [options]

Options:
  -o, --output PATH       Output JSONL path (required). Sidecar is <output>.scrubbed.
  -c, --config PATH       Rules YAML. Default: ./.ccs-sanitize.yaml or alongside input.
      --dry-run           Scan and print the sidecar to stdout; write nothing.
      --force             Allow overwriting an existing output file (default: refuse).
      --strip-types LIST  Line types dropped wholesale (§6b). Default:
                          file-history-snapshot,attachment.
  -v, --verbose           Per-rule progress to stderr.
      --version           Print sanitizer version.
```

**Exit codes (fail-closed):**

| Code | Meaning | Output written? |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Success | yes (+ sidecar) |
| 1 | Usage error (bad args, missing input, output exists without `--force`) | no |
| 2 | **Safety failure** — rule raised, line failed to parse, or residual scan found a secret | **no** |
| 3 | Config error (YAML invalid, regex won't compile, attempt to disable a built-in pattern) | no |

**Atomicity & rename order (I-5).** Output and sidecar are written to temp files in the
destination directory and renamed into place only after the full file is processed *and* the
residual scan passes. The **sidecar is renamed first, then the output** — so a crash in the
gap can leave an orphan sidecar (harmless, and overwritten on re-run) but can never leave a
scrubbed output with no sidecar, which would otherwise pass a sidecar-existence check while
being unaccounted for. A failed or interrupted run never leaves a partial scrub.

**Serialization is pinned for determinism (I-1).** Output lines are re-emitted with
`json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))` and **original key order preserved**
(Python's `json.loads` keeps insertion order, so a straight round-trip is
order-stable; keys are *not* sorted). Pinning these parameters is what turns "deterministic
output" from a claim into a property — without it, two environments could emit byte-different
but semantically equal output and break the determinism and idempotency tests.

**Malformed JSONL aborts (no skip flag in v0).** A session file should be well-formed; a parse
error means something is wrong, so the safe action is to stop. No `--skip-malformed` escape
hatch ships in v0 — adding a way to silently drop lines is a footgun on a security tool.

**The CLI is the sanctioned reader of raw sessions.** The [`block_secret_reads.py`](../../.claude/hooks/block_secret_reads.py)
hook blocks `Read`/`Edit`/`Grep`/`Glob` on `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` but deliberately
**not Bash** — so `ccs-sanitize ~/.claude/projects/.../sess.jsonl -o fixtures/sanitized/...`,
invoked via Bash, is the intended path for turning a raw session into a committable fixture.

---

## 12. Packaging & configuration

### Packaging — in-repo only for v0

**Decision D-5: in-repo only for v0; not published to PyPI.** Per the roadmap. A `pyproject.toml`
with a `ccs-sanitize` entry point lives at `tooling/sanitizer/`, uv-managed. Dependencies are
kept minimal: stdlib for the pipeline and secret patterns (mirroring the hooks' stdlib-only
constraint), plus PyYAML for config parsing. Target Python 3.11+. Extraction to a standalone
PyPI package (`claude-code-sessions-sanitizer`) is deferred until a standalone audience
materializes — the module layout is kept import-clean so extraction is mechanical later.

### Config model — hybrid {#config-model-hybrid}

**Decision D-1: hybrid.** Secret patterns are **code-defined** (the non-weakenable security
floor); path and identifier rules are **YAML-configured per project** (`.ccs-sanitize.yaml`).
YAML may *add* secret patterns (`extra_secret_patterns`) but never remove built-ins.

Rationale: a security tool whose secret detection can be silently weakened by editing a config
file is a tool that will eventually be weakened by a careless edit. Keeping the floor in code
means the worst a bad config can do is over-scrub (safe) or fail to add a project-specific
path rule (visible in the sidecar counts), never under-detect a secret.

Full config schema:

```yaml
version: 1
paths:        [ {match: "...", replace: "..."}, ... ]   # ordered, first-match-wins
identifiers:  [ {match: "...", replace: "..."}, ... ]
options:
  scrub_git_branch: true
  remap_uuids: false
extra_secret_patterns:                                   # ADDITIVE only
  - {pattern: "re:CORP-[A-Z0-9]{32}", kind: "corp-token"}
```

---

## 13. Fixture-validator integration

**Decision D-4: the validator re-scans independently and never trusts the sidecar.**

When [`tooling/fixture-validator/`](../../tooling/fixture-validator/README.md) checks a file
in `fixtures/sanitized/`, it:

1. Confirms a `.scrubbed` sidecar exists and its `sanitizer_version` is recognized.
2. **Independently re-runs the secret-pattern scan** over the fixture contents.
3. Optionally verifies `input_sha256` shape and required sidecar keys.

The validator does *not* trust the sidecar's `residual_scan: clean` as proof — it re-derives
it. This is defense in depth: a stale sidecar (output edited after scrub), a forged sidecar, or
a sanitizer bug all get caught at the validator layer. The cost is a cheap second regex pass;
the benefit is that fixture safety does not depend on the sanitizer having been bug-free at
scrub time. The "hybrid / trust counts" option was rejected — re-scanning is cheap enough that
there's no reason to trust *any* part of the security claim.

---

## 14. Testing strategy

Known-bad inputs live in `tests/fixtures/`. **They are synthetic and contain pattern-matching-but-fake secrets**
(e.g. `sk-ant-` followed by 25 `A`s) — never a real key.
This is itself a security requirement: the test suite must not be the thing that commits a
real credential.

Coverage:

- **Per-surface scrub tests** — a fixture line carrying each: home dir, project slug, absolute
  path, email, git branch with a ticket ID, and each Tier-1 and Tier-2 secret pattern. Assert
  the output contains none of the original tokens and the sidecar counts are correct.
- **Structural-traversal test (C-1)** — secrets/paths planted in *nested* leaves the line-level
  view hides (`tool_use.input.command`, `toolUseResult.stdout`, `tool_result.content` array
  shape, `message.content[].text`); assert all are scrubbed and skip-list fields
  (`message.model`, `usage.*`, `thinking.signature`) are untouched.
- **Strip-types test (C-2/D-7)** — input with `file-history-snapshot` and `attachment` lines;
  assert they are dropped, counted in `stripped_lines`, and no `trackedFileBackups` content
  survives anywhere in the output.
- **Residual-scan / fail-closed test** — craft an input where naive redaction could be bypassed
  (a secret split across a transform boundary); assert the residual scan catches it, the run
  exits 2, and no output file exists.
- **No-partial-scrub test** — induce a rule error mid-file; assert no output and no sidecar.
- **Determinism test** — same input + config → byte-identical output across two runs (pins the
  serialization parameters from [§11](#11-cli-shape--fail-closed-behavior)).
- **Idempotency test** — sanitizing an already-sanitized file is a no-op (0 substitutions,
  `residual_scan: clean`).
- **Sidecar-never-leaks test** — assert no original sensitive token (home dir, email, secret)
  *and no configured replacement that is itself sensitive* appears anywhere in the sidecar (I-3).
- **Pattern-sync test** (repo-level) — normalize the hook's compiled `SECRET_PATTERNS` via
  `.pattern` and assert element-wise equality with `VENDORED_PATTERNS` (drift guard from §9);
  `BATCH_PATTERNS` excluded.

---

## 15. Open questions — resolutions

Every open question from [`tooling/sanitizer/README.md`](../../tooling/sanitizer/README.md)
and the [epic](https://github.com/real-user/claude-code-sessions/issues/1),
with its resolution. All resolved 2026-05-29.

| # | Source | Question | Resolution | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | README | YAML-configured vs code-defined rules | **Hybrid** — secrets in code (additive-only YAML extension), paths/identifiers in YAML | [D-1](#decision-d-1--rule-configuration-is-hybrid) |
| 2 | README | Sidecar: substitution dictionaries vs counts | **Redacted per-substitution detail**; secrets count-only; no original values | [D-2](#decision-d-2--redacted-sidecar) |
| 3 | README | Jitter granularity (field/message/session) | **Deferred to v1**; designed as per-session offset | [D-3](#9b-layer-4-jitter-deferred-to-v1-but-designed) |
| 4 | README | Validator: re-scan vs trust sidecar | **Independent re-scan**, never trust the sidecar | [D-4](#13-fixture-validator-integration) |
| 5 | Roadmap | PyPI package vs in-repo | **In-repo only for v0** | [D-5](#packaging--in-repo-only-for-v0) |
| 6 | Roadmap | Secret-pattern library: copy vs dependency | **Vendor (copy)** into the sanitizer; sync-test guards drift | [D-6](#decision-d-6--vendor-the-secret-pattern-library) |
| 7 | Review | High-risk line types (`file-history-snapshot`, `attachment`) | **Dropped wholesale in v0** via `--strip-types`; synthetic fixtures cover those surfaces | [D-7](#decision-d-7--v0-drops-high-risk-line-types) |

### Decision D-1 — rule configuration is hybrid
Secrets code-defined (non-weakenable floor, additive YAML extension allowed); paths/identifiers
in YAML. A config-weakenable security floor will eventually be weakened by accident; keeping it
in code means a bad config can only over-scrub or miss a path rule, never under-detect a secret.

### Decision D-2 — redacted sidecar
Per-substitution detail using category placeholders and the (non-sensitive) replacement value;
secrets contribute a count only; no original values anywhere. Keeps the sidecar auditable
without making it a second copy of the data we just scrubbed.

### Decision D-6 — vendor the secret-pattern library
This repo is **upstream** of AgentFluent (per [CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) and the data
dictionary). Taking a runtime dependency on AgentFluent would invert that relationship. The
pattern set is therefore copied into `rules/secrets.py`, which becomes a candidate canonical
home; a future task can have the hook and/or AgentFluent consume from here. A repo-level
sync-test prevents the vendored Tier-1 copy and the hook's copy from drifting in the meantime.

### Decision D-7 — v0 drops high-risk line types
`file-history-snapshot` (full file contents in `trackedFileBackups`) and `attachment` (opaque
binary/image payloads) cannot be credibly scrubbed with pattern rules. v0 drops them wholesale
(`--strip-types`, counted in the sidecar) rather than ship a false sense of safety. Surfaces
that need those line types in a fixture are built synthetically. Content-level scrubbing is
future work ([§17](#17-future-work-v1)). Surfaced by architect review (C-2), 2026-05-29.

---

## 16. Phasing & acceptance criteria

**Phase 1 (this document):** PRD accepted. Done when every open question in §15 is resolved
and the design is signed off.

**Phase 2 (implementation):** acceptance criteria from the [epic](https://github.com/real-user/claude-code-sessions/issues/1):

- [ ] CLI usable as `ccs-sanitize <input.jsonl> -o <output.jsonl>`
- [ ] Strip-types step drops `file-history-snapshot`/`attachment` (§6b); structural traversal
      with skip-list reaches nested leaves (§6b)
- [ ] Layered rules: paths → identifiers → secrets (jitter stub present, disabled)
- [ ] `.scrubbed` sidecar in the redacted format of §10
- [ ] Fails closed: any rule error or residual secret aborts; no partial scrubs
- [ ] Test suite covers the known-bad inputs of §14

{"body":"**Epic:** #5

## Summary

Migrate the JSONL format documentation from AgentFluent's CLAUDE.md ("JSONL Data Format" section) into `reference/data-dictionary.md`, replacing the current TODO skeletons with authoritative, version-stamped content. This is the largest single piece of the reference migration.

**Roadmap reference:** See [`.claude/specs/roadmap-v0.md` (W3)](https://github.com/real-user/claude-code-sessions/blob/main/.claude/specs/roadmap-v0.md#w3--migrate-jsonl-format-docs-from-agentfluents-claudemd--reference).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All TODO sections in `reference/data-dictionary.md` populated with content migrated from AgentFluent's CLAUDE.md:
  - File location (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl` convention, slug derivation, per-project subdirectories, subagent trace subdirectories, file rotation)
  - Common fields (`type`, `timestamp`, `uuid`, `parentUuid`, `sessionId`, `isSidechain`, `cwd`, `version`)
  - Message types: `assistant` (message.role, message.model, message.content, message.usage, message.stop_reason)
  - Message types: `user` (two shapes of message.content, tool_result blocks, toolUseResult envelope)
  - Skipped types (`file-history-snapshot`, `progress`, `hook_progress`, `bash_progress`, `system`, `create`)
  - Content blocks: `text`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, `thinking`
  - Usage and token accounting (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`)
  - Hook event fields

Slice **Phase 2** of the sanitizer epic into discrete, well-scoped child-story issues and file them on GitHub. 1. **Scaffold** — `tooling/sanitizer/pyproject.toml`, `src/ccs_sanitize/` skeleton, uv config, smoke-test that `ccs-sanitize --version` runs. No real logic.

39	└── README.md
40	```
41	
42	Likely published as `claude-code-sessions-sanitizer` (or short alias like `ccs-sanitize`) once stable.
43	
44	## Rule sources
45	
46	- **Path/identifier scrubbing** — bespoke to this project; rules configurable per-project via a yaml file
47	- **Secret-pattern detection** — reuse the pattern library from [AgentFluent's `detect_secrets_in_output.py`](https://github.com/real-user/agentfluent/blob/main/.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py) (Anthropic API keys, GitHub PATs, AWS keys, Google API keys, etc.)
48

51	Every scrubbed output file gets a `<filename>.scrubbed` sidecar:
52	
53	```yaml

56	scrubbed_at: 2026-MM-DD
57	rules_applied:
58	  - paths: 14 substitutions
59	  - identifiers: 3 substitutions
60	  - secrets: 0 matches
61	  - jitter: disabled
