fix(sanitizer): apply /simplify review pass on pipeline core (#20)

Applies the 13 confirmed findings from a /simplify review of PR #30
(pipeline core for ccs-sanitize). All correctness bugs were caught by
either the line-by-line angle, the removed-behavior auditor, the
cross-file tracer, or the Python-pitfall specialist; the cleanups by
the simplification/reuse/altitude angles.

Correctness fixes
-----------------

- default_skip_predicate over-skipped bare `id`/`signature`/`model`
  field names anywhere they appeared, exempting user-controlled content
  like MCP `tool_use.input.id` from scrubbing. PRD section 6b B anchors
  these to specific parent paths (message.model, message.id,
  tool_use.id under message.content[*], thinking.signature under
  message.content[*]). The predicate now uses a (parent, last) anchor
  set for those four fields and keeps the bare-name skip only for
  PRD-listed names that don't collide with user-data field names.

- `"usage" in path` was a membership-anywhere check that would skip any
  descendant of any field literally named `usage` at any depth — over-
  broad relative to PRD §6b B which scopes the skip to usage.* (the
  token-accounting block). Replaced with an immediate-parent check
  (path[-2] == "usage").

- run_pipeline now fail-closes on shape violations: a non-object JSONL
  root (bare string/number/array — would otherwise bypass the
  strip-types gate and be silently walked), a missing `type` field, or
  a non-string `type` field (e.g., `{"type": ["attachment"]}` trying to
  smuggle an attachment past the strip). PRD §11 frames these as
  malformed input the security tool should refuse rather than tolerate.

- PipelineError messages now reference the 1-indexed *input* line
  number rather than the post-filter record index. Blank lines preceding
  a malformed line shifted the reported index; users couldn't locate
  the bad line in their source file.

- SubstitutionTable.__iter__ now snapshots the entries via list(...)
  before yielding, so a transform that calls record() mid-iteration
  doesn't raise RuntimeError on the next __next__. The sidecar consumer
  (#25) is a natural caller of this pattern.

- serialize_line now passes allow_nan=False. NaN/Infinity in the parsed
  tree would otherwise emit non-RFC-8259 JSON; strict downstream parsers
  reject those tokens. Surfaces as PipelineError so the CLI maps it to
  exit code 2 (safety failure).

- PipelineCounts.stripped_lines is now a MappingProxyType. The frozen
  dataclass blocked __setattr__ but the inner dict was a shared
  reference; a caller could silently corrupt the sidecar's tallies.

Docstring fix
-------------

- serialize_line previously claimed "the round-trip is byte-stable for
  byte-stable input". False for any numeric literal that json.dumps
  normalizes (e.g., 1e10 → 10000000000.0). The actually-achievable claim
  is two runs over the same parsed Python object produce byte-identical
  output — the determinism contract the residual scan and validator
  depend on. Strict source-byte preservation is not a goal and is not
  needed by anything downstream.

Forward-compat addition
-----------------------

- make_skip_predicate(*, remap_uuids=False) factory. PRD §6b B says UUID
  fields are skipped "unless remap_uuids is on", but the previous
  predicate hardcoded UUID names so #19's ConfigOptions.remap_uuids
  could not influence them. #22 (identifiers layer) will pass
  remap_uuids=True from the loaded config and get a predicate that
  visits UUID fields so they can be remapped consistently. The
  default_skip_predicate is now `make_skip_predicate()` and existing
  call sites are unchanged.

Cleanups
--------

- walk_strings recursion moved into a nested helper; the public
  signature no longer exposes the leading-underscore `_path` keyword
  that callers (or **kwargs forwarders) could accidentally pass.

- SubstitutionTable internal storage moved from dict[str, list[object]]
  with four # type: ignore markers to dict[str, _Row] where _Row is a
  small mutable dataclass. No public behavior change; the `Entry`
  frozen view is unchanged.

- Test helper _line() delegates to serialize_line rather than
  reimplementing it minus ensure_ascii=False. A future pinning change
  in serialize_line will now propagate automatically.

Deferred
--------

One finding is acknowledged in the docstring but not fixed in this PR:
PRD §2 says thinking.signature is "Replaced with a fixed placeholder
(no analytical value in a fixture)", but the current implementation
skip-lists it (pass-through). The placeholder substitution is a
separate architectural step (a fixed-replacement layer that runs
before rule transforms) that belongs in a focused later PR rather than
mixed into this review pass. The pass-through is safe — the residual
scan's pattern set doesn't false-positive on signature shapes — but
it's PRD-incomplete.

Tests
-----

44 passed, 1 expected skip (the CLI smoke from #18 skips when
ccs-sanitize isn't on the parent shell's PATH). New tests cover:

- bare id/signature/model in user-controlled content IS visited
- user-named 'usage' field IS visited (not over-skipped)
- genuine usage subtree (message.usage.service_tier) still skipped
- non-dict roots, missing type, non-string type all raise PipelineError
- error messages name the input line number
- make_skip_predicate(remap_uuids=True) visits UUID fields
- NaN and Infinity in serialize_line raise PipelineError
- PipelineCounts.stripped_lines rejects mutation
- SubstitutionTable.__iter__ tolerates concurrent record() calls

**Scope:** PR #29 at `feature/19-config-loader`, checked out at `/home/user/Documents/Projects/git/claude-code-sessions`. Fetch with `git diff main...HEAD`.

PR #29 lands typed dataclasses (`Config`, `Rule`, `ExtraSecretPattern`, `ConfigOptions`) that wrap user YAML input, plus the I-3 replacement-leak guard that traverses these wrappers.

**What to find:**

1. **`Rule.compiled: re.Pattern[str]`** — the field is the "wrapped" matcher. Look at how `_check_replacement_leak` uses it: `other.compiled.search(rule.replace)`. For literal rules, `compiled` is `re.compile(re.escape(literal))`. So `compiled.search(replace_value)` returns a match if `literal` appears anywhere in `replace_value`. This is essentially `literal in replace_value` (substring check). But — is `re.search` slower than `in` here? More importantly: is there a case where `re.escape(literal)` does NOT exactly correspond to substring matching? E.g., if the literal contains characters that have multibyte representations in some weirdness, does this break?

2. **`Rule.is_regex` field** — exposes whether the rule was originally written with `re:` prefix. Future rule layers will branch on it. Is this field's value EVER read in this PR? If not, it's a wrapper interface design choice waiting to bear fruit (#21, #22). Verify the value is set correctly for both branches of `_compile_rule`.

3. **The `_compile_rule(pattern_str, replace, *, where) -> Rule` factory** — it wraps a (pattern, replace) input pair. Cleanly forwards `where` only for error messages. Does it preserve all the inputs accurately? The `Rule.pattern` stores the original YAML value (with `re:` prefix); is this what callers need?

4. **`ExtraSecretPattern` vs `Rule`** — two wrapper types for similar concepts. `Rule` has both `pattern` and `replace`; `ExtraSecretPattern` has `pattern` and `kind` (no replace, since secrets are redacted not remapped). Are these intentionally different shapes, or is there an opportunity for a shared base?

5. **The substitution-table semantics in #29 don't apply** — this PR has no SubstitutionTable wrapper, but the I-3 guard's own loop is wrapper-like: it iterates `all_rules` of `(section, rule)` pairs. Does anything in that traversal mutate state that's observed by later iterations? (No — purely read-only.) Verify.

6. **`Config` is frozen** but the field types include lists. `Config(version=1, paths=[r], identifiers=[r], ...)` — can a caller mutate `config.paths.append(other_rule)` after construction? Yes, because `field(default_factory=list)` doesn't make the list itself immutable. Worth flagging if downstream code (e.g., the future rule-layer adapters) might mutate.

7. **`_check_replacement_leak` self-skip** — `if other is rule: continue`. This is identity comparison. Builds `all_rules` once as a fresh list of `(section, rule)` tuples. The `rule` and `other` are bound to the actual `Rule` instances in `config.paths`/`config.identifiers`. Identity holds. But — what if `config.paths` contained two `Rule` instances that are `==` but not `is`? Is that even possible from a YAML config? (Yes, in theory — two identical entries.) Are two identical rules in a config a legitimate error or a no-op? The current `is` check would skip only the literal self, not the duplicate.

1. `git diff main...HEAD`
2. Full bodies of `config.py`, `rules/secrets.py`, `tests/test_config.py`

You are running the **Altitude** review angle for PR #29.

**Scope:** PR #29 at `feature/19-config-loader`, checked out at `/home/user/Documents/Projects/git/claude-code-sessions`. Fetch with `git diff main...HEAD`.

The PR introduces the YAML config loader, the I-3 replacement-leak guard, and the secret-pattern constants. It will be extended by future PRs:
- #21 (paths layer): consumes `Config.paths` and applies them via rules.
- #22 (identifiers layer): consumes `Config.identifiers`, `ConfigOptions.scrub_git_branch`, `ConfigOptions.remap_uuids`.
- #23 (secrets layer): consumes `SECRET_PATTERNS` + `Config.extra_secret_patterns`, and ships the I-4 sync test.

**What to find:** Check that each change is at the right depth, not a fragile bandaid.

1. **`_REGEX_PREFIX = "re:"` as the way to switch a YAML `match:` between literal and regex.** Is this the right level of abstraction? Alternatives: a separate `regex:` key, a `type: literal | regex` field, or YAML tag (`!regex pattern`). The `re:` prefix is convenient but is a string-level marker that a future user could trip on (e.g., a literal that happens to start with `re:`). Is this PRD-mandated or implementation choice?

2. **`Config` is frozen** but field lists are mutable. Should the lists themselves be tuples (immutable) so the entire `Config` is structurally immutable? Or should `Config` expose a `freeze()` step?

3. **`ConfigError` is a `ValueError` subclass.** This is fine for the local layer, but at the CLI boundary (#26) it gets caught and mapped to exit code 3. Is the mapping going to be straightforward, or will the CLI need to introspect specific subclasses for better diagnostics? (E.g., `ConfigSchemaError`, `ConfigRegexError`, `ConfigLeakError`.)

4. **`SECRET_PATTERNS` lives in `rules/secrets.py`** — a layer module. The I-3 guard in `config.py` imports it. This means `config.py` depends on a rule module. Is that the right dependency direction? An alternative: keep patterns in a neutral "registry" module and have both `config.py` and the future `rules/secrets.py` scrub logic import from there. Today's structure works, but is it future-proof?

5. **`ExtraSecretPattern` has `pattern` (the raw user-supplied string) and `compiled` (the precompiled regex).** Future rule layers will iterate and apply. But: extras land alongside built-ins in #23's scrub logic. Where will the merge happen? If `config.py` returns a Config carrying just the extras, #23's scrub function will need to concatenate. Is that the right shape, or should `load_config` return a single `effective_secret_patterns: list[Pattern]` that #23 just iterates?

6. **The I-3 guard's loop traverses path-rules and identifier-rules and checks each replacement against (a) other rules and (b) built-in/extra secret patterns. Is the loop the right depth?** Alternative: build a single "all patterns" set once and check each replacement once. The current form has error-specific messages per cause (more debuggable); the consolidated form would lose that.

7. **PRD §10 sidecar shape** — `substitutions: [{rule, placeholder, replacement, occurrences}]`. Does `Config` carry enough state for the sidecar to attribute substitutions to layers? Or does that bookkeeping live entirely in the future rule layers? The Config returns the rules as-is; the layer is implicit. Is that the right altitude?

8. **`Rule.is_regex`** — exposing this as a stored field communicates "the rule's original shape matters to callers". Is that true, or is it an implementation detail that future callers should not branch on? If they should branch (e.g., for sidecar reporting "literal path /home/x", "regex /home/.*"), the field is the right shape. If they shouldn't, it's noise.

This is an architecture angle. `failure_scenario` should state the concrete cost (e.g., "#21 will need to do X, which the current API doesn't support").

**Required reading:**
1. `git diff main...HEAD`
2. Full bodies of `config.py`, `rules/secrets.py`, `tests/test_config.py`
3. PRD `.claude/specs/prd-sanitizer.md` — full re-read
4. Sibling PR #30 diff for cross-cutting

**Output:** JSON array of up to 8 findings `{file, line, summary, failure_scenario}`. Return ONLY JSON.

PRD §11 contract relies on the CLI not collapsing them.

4. **`extra_secret_patterns` pattern semantics differ from `paths`/`identifiers`** — path/identifier rules without `re:` prefix get `re.escape` applied (literal); extras secret patterns without `re:` are compiled raw (regex). A user writing `pattern: "C++"` in extras hits a `ConfigError` for invalid regex; the same string in `paths.match` would be a valid literal. Inconsistent UX, and the docstring doesn't note the asymmetry.

The contract is sound (skip-list is "things NOT to scrub"; `gitBranch` is visited; the layer #22 transform handles it) but the dependency is undocumented.

"""YAML config loader for path/identifier rules and additive secret patterns.

PRD reference:

  - section 12 — hybrid config model (D-1). Secrets are code-defined and
    non-weakenable; paths and identifiers are YAML-configured per project;
    ``extra_secret_patterns`` is additive only.
  - section 10 — the sidecar reproduces ``replace`` values verbatim, so a
    misconfigured rule whose replacement is itself sensitive would leak
    through the sidecar (I-3). ``load_config`` runs the replacement-leak
    guard at load time: any path/identifier ``replace`` that matches any
    other path rule (including itself), any identifier rule, or any built-in /
    extra secret pattern is rejected with a typed error.

CLI wiring (translating ``ConfigError`` to exit code 3 per PRD section 11)
lands with #26. A missing config file surfaces as ``FileNotFoundError`` and
maps to exit 1 (usage error) at the CLI layer; other I/O or decoding errors
from the loader are normalized to ``ConfigError`` so the CLI can distinguish
them cleanly.

The YAML schema uses ``match:`` per the PRD; the Python field is named
``pattern`` to avoid visual collision with Python's ``match``/``case``
statement.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import yaml

from .rules.secrets import SECRET_PATTERNS

_SUPPORTED_VERSION = 1
_REGEX_PREFIX = "re:"

_ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"version", "paths", "identifiers", "options", "extra_secret_patterns"}
)
_ALLOWED_RULE_KEYS = frozenset({"match", "replace"})
_ALLOWED_OPTION_KEYS = frozenset({"scrub_git_branch", "remap_uuids"})
_ALLOWED_EXTRA_KEYS = frozenset({"pattern", "kind"})

# Compile built-in secret patterns once at module import. This (a) catches a
# typo in a vendored or batch pattern at import time rather than on first
# config load, and (b) amortizes the per-load compile cost into a single
# upfront step.
_BUILTIN_COMPILED: list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], str]] = [
    (re.compile(pat), label) for pat, label in SECRET_PATTERNS
]


class ConfigError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a config file fails to load or validate.

    Maps to CLI exit code 3 (PRD section 11) when caught at the CLI layer.
    The message names the offending field/rule so a human reviewer can fix
    it without digging.
    """


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Rule:
    """A path or identifier rule.

    ``pattern`` is the YAML ``match:`` value as written (with the ``re:``
    prefix preserved if regex). ``compiled`` is the regex used for matching:

      - Literal rules compile to ``re.escape(pattern)`` so the I-3 guard and
        future scrub layers can use one ``re.Pattern`` code path.
      - Regex rules compile the substring after ``re:``.

    ``__post_init__`` validates that ``compiled`` and ``is_regex`` are
    consistent with ``pattern``, so direct ``Rule(...)`` construction
    (the type is public via ``__all__``) cannot produce a desynced object
    that the I-3 guard would silently miscompare against.
    """

    pattern: str
    replace: str
    is_regex: bool
    compiled: re.Pattern[str]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        expected_is_regex = self.pattern.startswith(_REGEX_PREFIX)
        expected_source = (
            self.pattern[len(_REGEX_PREFIX) :]
            if expected_is_regex
            else re.escape(self.pattern)
        )
        if self.is_regex != expected_is_regex:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Rule.is_regex={self.is_regex} does not match pattern={self.pattern!r}"
            )
        if self.compiled.pattern != expected_source:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Rule.compiled.pattern={self.compiled.pattern!r} does not match "
                f"expected {expected_source!r} derived from pattern={self.pattern!r}"
            )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ExtraSecretPattern:
    """A user-supplied additive secret pattern (PRD section 9).

    Schema parity with ``Rule``: bare ``pattern`` strings are treated as
    literals (escaped to a regex), strings prefixed with ``re:`` are
    compiled as regex — matching how paths and identifiers behave. The
    earlier version of this loader compiled bare strings raw, which created
    surprising semantics for users writing ``pattern: "C++"`` or similar.
    """

    pattern: str
    kind: str
    compiled: re.Pattern[str]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.pattern.startswith(_REGEX_PREFIX):
            expected_source = self.pattern[len(_REGEX_PREFIX) :]
        else:
            expected_source = re.escape(self.pattern)
        if self.compiled.pattern != expected_source:
            raise ValueError(
                f"ExtraSecretPattern.compiled.pattern={self.compiled.pattern!r} does not "
                f"match expected {expected_source!r} derived from pattern={self.pattern!r}"
            )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ConfigOptions:
    scrub_git_branch: bool = True
    remap_uuids: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Config:
    """Validated, immutable config tree.

    Field lists (``paths``, ``identifiers``, ``extra_secret_patterns``) are
    converted to tuples in ``__post_init__`` so that ``Config`` is
    structurally immutable. A frozen dataclass with mutable ``list`` fields
    would allow downstream code to ``config.paths.append(...)`` post-
    validation, bypassing the I-3 replacement-leak guard that ran at load
    time. Tuples keep the iteration ergonomics callers expect while
    blocking that bypass.
    """

    version: int
    paths: tuple[Rule, ...] = ()
    identifiers: tuple[Rule, ...] = ()
    options: ConfigOptions = field(default_factory=ConfigOptions)
    extra_secret_patterns: tuple[ExtraSecretPattern, ...] = ()

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # Accept lists at construction time (the loader builds lists), but
        # store as tuples so the public surface is immutable.
        if not isinstance(self.paths, tuple):
            object.__setattr__(self, "paths", tuple(self.paths))
        if not isinstance(self.identifiers, tuple):
            object.__setattr__(self, "identifiers", tuple(self.identifiers))
        if not isinstance(self.extra_secret_patterns, tuple):
            object.__setattr__(
                self, "extra_secret_patterns", tuple(self.extra_secret_patterns)
            )


def load_config(path: Path | str) -> Config:
    """Load and validate a sanitizer config file.

    The path's ``~`` prefix is expanded so callers can pass
    ``~/.ccs-sanitize.yaml`` without pre-expansion. Read errors and
    decode errors are normalized to ``ConfigError`` so the CLI layer
    sees a single error class for every config-stage failure other than
    "file does not exist".

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: the path does not exist (CLI maps to exit 1).

                    f"{other_section} rule match {other.pattern!r} — "

"""Tests for the YAML config loader (issue #19).

Covers:

  - Loading a valid config returns the expected ``Config`` shape.
  - Malformed YAML raises ``ConfigError`` (not ``yaml.YAMLError``).
  - Schema violations (unknown keys, wrong types, missing required fields,
    invalid regex) raise ``ConfigError`` with a message that names the offender.
  - The I-3 replacement-leak guard rejects replacements that themselves match
    any path, identifier, or built-in/extra secret rule.
  - The Tier-1 and Tier-2 secret-pattern constants are present and compile.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from ccs_sanitize.config import (
    ConfigError,
    ConfigOptions,
    load_config,
)
from ccs_sanitize.rules.secrets import (
    BATCH_PATTERNS,
    SECRET_PATTERNS,
    VENDORED_PATTERNS,
)


def _write(tmp_path: Path, body: str) -> Path:
    p = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
    p.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
    return p


# ----- happy paths --------------------------------------------------------


def test_minimal_valid_config(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = load_config(_write(tmp_path, "version: 1\n"))
    assert config.version == 1
    assert config.paths == []
    assert config.identifiers == []
    assert config.options == ConfigOptions()
    assert config.extra_secret_patterns == []

def test_full_valid_config(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    body = """
version: 1
paths:
  - match: "/home/user"
    replace: "/home/user"
  - match: "re:-home-user-([a-z0-9-]+)"
    replace: "-home-user-project"
identifiers:
  - match: "user@example.com"
    replace: "user@example.com"
options:
  scrub_git_branch: true
  remap_uuids: false
extra_secret_patterns:
  - pattern: "re:CORP-[A-Z0-9]{32}"
    kind: "corp-token"
"""
    config = load_config(_write(tmp_path, body))
    assert config.version == 1
    assert len(config.paths) == 2
    assert config.paths[0].pattern == "/home/user"
    assert config.paths[0].is_regex is False
    assert config.paths[1].is_regex is True
    assert config.identifiers[0].replace == "user@example.com"
    assert config.options.scrub_git_branch is True
    assert config.options.remap_uuids is False
    assert len(config.extra_secret_patterns) == 1

def test_secret_pattern_labels_are_unique() -> None:
    labels = [label for _, label in SECRET_PATTERNS]
    assert len(labels) == len(set(labels)), f"duplicate labels: {labels}"


def test_pem_pattern_catches_encrypted_private_key() -> None:
    """Standard PKCS#8 encrypted PEM headers (what openssl pkcs8 and
    passphrase-protected ssh-keygen produce) must match the PEM pattern;
    an earlier version of the regex only listed the unencrypted variants."""
    import re as _re

    pem_pattern = next(p for p, label in BATCH_PATTERNS if label == "pem-private-key")
    compiled = _re.compile(pem_pattern)
    assert compiled.search("<REDACTED:pem-private-key>") is not None
    assert compiled.search("<REDACTED:pem-private-key>") is not None
    assert compiled.search("<REDACTED:pem-private-key>") is not None

def test_version_bool_rejected(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """``version: true`` in YAML parses to Python ``True``; without the
    isinstance gate ``True == 1`` would silently accept it (and the
    sidecar would later serialize a bool)."""
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="version must be an integer"):
        load_config(_write(tmp_path, "version: true\n"))


def test_version_float_rejected(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """``version: 1.0`` compares equal to ``1`` but is a float; reject so
    the sidecar's sanitizer_version stays integer-typed."""
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="version must be an integer"):
        load_config(_write(tmp_path, "version: 1.0\n"))


def test_version_string_rejected(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="version must be an integer"):
        load_config(_write(tmp_path, 'version: "1"\n'))


def test_extra_secret_pattern_re_prefix_empty_raises(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """``pattern: "re:"`` is empty after the prefix strip; ``re.compile("")``
    silently succeeds and matches every position, so we must reject it
    the same way ``_compile_rule`` does for paths/identifiers."""
    body = """
version: 1
extra_secret_patterns:
  - pattern: "re:"
    kind: "oops"
"""
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="empty regex"):
        load_config(_write(tmp_path, body))


def test_extra_secret_pattern_bare_string_is_literal(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Bare ``pattern`` strings in extras are treated as literals (escaped),
    matching how paths and identifiers handle bare ``match:`` values. The
    earlier loader compiled bare strings raw, so ``pattern: "C++"`` was
    silently a regex with a quantifier."""
    body = """
version: 1
extra_secret_patterns:
  - pattern: "C++"
    kind: "lang-tag"
"""
    config = load_config(_write(tmp_path, body))
    extra = config.extra_secret_patterns[0]
    # Literal compile: source pattern is re.escape("C++").
    assert extra.compiled.pattern == re.escape("C++")
    # The literal substring matches; the would-be regex 'C++' (one+ Cs)
    # would have matched a bare "C" too — verify it does NOT under our
    # literal interpretation.
    assert extra.compiled.search("C++") is not None
    assert extra.compiled.search("C") is None


def test_i3_self_rule_replace_contains_own_match(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """A rule whose own ``replace`` contains its own ``match`` is non-
    idempotent (a second pass would re-substitute) and leaks the original
    pattern through the sidecar. The earlier guard skipped the self-
    comparison and let this through."""
    body = """
version: 1
paths:
  - match: "/home/user"
    replace: "/home/user-redacted"
"""
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="not.+idempotent|own match"):
        load_config(_write(tmp_path, body))


def test_config_paths_are_immutable_tuple(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Config(frozen=True) only blocks attribute reassignment; ensure the
    field types are tuples so callers cannot ``.append`` to bypass the
    I-3 guard post-validation."""
    body = """
version: 1
paths:
  - match: "/home/user"
    replace: "/home/user"
"""
    config = load_config(_write(tmp_path, body))
    assert isinstance(config.paths, tuple)
    assert isinstance(config.identifiers, tuple)
    assert isinstance(config.extra_secret_patterns, tuple)
    # And mutation attempts fail:
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
        config.paths.append(config.paths[0])  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

    """``Path("~/...")`` does not auto-expand; load_config must expand so a
    quoted ``~/.ccs-sanitize.yaml`` from the CLI works."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("HOME", str(tmp_path))

    # Reference the file via tilde-prefixed string.

    p = tmp_path / "config.yaml"

def test_options_defaults_only_apply_when_key_omitted(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """When the YAML sets an option explicitly, that value wins; defaults
    only fill in for omitted keys. Earlier the loader duplicated defaults
    in both the dataclass and ``_build_options``, which would silently
    disagree if the dataclass default changed."""

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed (review pass on issue #19)
- **PEM private-key pattern now catches `ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY`** (standard
  PKCS#8 encrypted PEM, the output of `openssl pkcs8` and passphrase-
  protected `ssh-keygen`). Previously only the unencrypted variants matched,
  so an encrypted private key in session output could slip past both scrubs
  and the residual scan.
- `extra_secret_patterns` now mirror path/identifier rule semantics: bare
  strings are treated as literals (`re.escape`'d), `re:`-prefixed strings
  are compiled as regex. The earlier loader compiled bare strings raw, so
  `pattern: "C++"` silently became a regex with a quantifier.
- `extra_secret_patterns` with `pattern: "re:"` now raises `ConfigError`
  (same guard `_compile_rule` has for paths/identifiers). The previous
  loader accepted the empty regex, which matches every position and would
  trip the I-3 guard against every rule.
- `version` is now type-checked. YAML `version: true` (parses to Python
  `True`) and `version: 1.0` were silently accepted because Python treats
  `True == 1` and `1.0 == 1`; the loader now requires an `int` that is
  not a `bool`.
- I-3 replacement-leak guard no longer skips the self-rule comparison,
  so a rule whose own `replace` contains its own `match` (a non-
  idempotent rule that would leak the original pattern through the
  sidecar) is rejected with a focused error.
- `Config` field lists (`paths`, `identifiers`, `extra_secret_patterns`)
  are converted to tuples in `__post_init__`. `@dataclass(frozen=True)`
  blocks attribute reassignment but not list mutation; with mutable lists,
  downstream code could `config.paths.append(...)` after `load_config`
  returned, bypassing the I-3 guard.
- `load_config(path)` now expands `~` in the input path. Quoted
  `--config '~/.ccs-sanitize.yaml'` from the CLI was previously raising
  `FileNotFoundError` against a literal tilde.
- `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` errors and other `OSError` from the read
  step are now wrapped in `ConfigError` so the CLI's (eventual)
  `ConfigError` → exit 3 mapping catches them; previously a Windows
  UTF-16-saved config would surface as a bare `UnicodeDecodeError` and
  bypass the documented exit-code contract.
- Empty YAML sections — `paths:`/`identifiers:`/`extra_secret_patterns:`
  with no value (parses to `None`) — are now treated as empty lists,
  matching how `options:` already handles `None`. Previously the loader
  raised `ConfigError("paths must be a list, got NoneType")` for an
  ergonomic shape that should mean "no rules".
- `_check_replacement_leak` now uses a module-level `_BUILTIN_COMPILED`
  table instead of recompiling `SECRET_PATTERNS` on every call. The
  table compiles at module import, so a future typo in a vendored or
  batch pattern surfaces at import time, not on first config load.

# Changelog — `claude-code-sessions-sanitizer`

All notable changes to this package will be documented here. The version
recorded in every `.scrubbed` sidecar (`sanitizer_version:` field, PRD section 10)
references this file.

## Bump policy

**Bump on any change that could alter the produced output bytes.** That
includes, non-exhaustively:

- New or modified path / identifier / secret rules.
- New entries in `VENDORED_PATTERNS` or `BATCH_PATTERNS`.
- Any change to the line-loop, the structural traversal skip-list, or the
  set of stripped line types.
- Changes to JSON serialization parameters (separators, key order, ASCII
  escaping) or the sidecar emission contract.
- Bug fixes in a regex that change which inputs match.

A bug fix that does **not** change which inputs match (e.g., refactoring a
helper, fixing an error message) does not require a bump.

The rule is conservative because the PRD's determinism contract — "same input
+ same config → byte-identical output" — only holds *within* a sanitizer
version. Downstream consumers (the fixture-validator, sibling projects) gate
on the sidecar's `sanitizer_version`. If the bytes change without the version,
the contract is meaningless.

Use semver: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.

- `PATCH` — bug fix that changes which inputs match a rule (no rule added or
  removed; no config-surface change).
- `MINOR` — new rule, new pattern, new CLI flag, new sidecar field. Backward
  compatible at the config-surface level.
- `MAJOR` — sidecar format change, config schema break, removal of a built-in
  pattern, or any change requiring re-running the sanitizer on previously
  scrubbed sessions.

## [Unreleased]

### Added (issue #19)
- YAML config loader at `ccs_sanitize.config.load_config`. Reads a `.ccs-sanitize.yaml`
  per PRD §12 schema and returns a typed `Config` (with `Rule`, `ExtraSecretPattern`,
  `ConfigOptions` sub-types). Surfaces `ConfigError` (a `ValueError` subclass) for
  malformed YAML, schema violations, invalid regex, attempts to add unknown keys, and
  I-3 replacement-leak failures. A missing file surfaces as `FileNotFoundError` so the
  CLI (#26) can map it to exit 1 distinct from `ConfigError` → exit 3 (PRD §11).
- Replacement-leak guard (I-3) at config load time: any path/identifier `replace:`
  value that matches any other path rule, any identifier rule, any built-in
  `SECRET_PATTERNS` entry, or any `extra_secret_patterns` regex is rejected with a
  message naming both the offending rule and the rule it leaked into.
- `VENDORED_PATTERNS` (Tier-1, copied verbatim from
  `.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py`) and `BATCH_PATTERNS` (Tier-2, the §9
  sanitizer-only additions: PEM keys, bearer tokens, JWTs, DB connection strings,
  Slack tokens) land in `rules/secrets.py` so the I-3 guard has something to validate
  against. `SECRET_PATTERNS = VENDORED_PATTERNS + BATCH_PATTERNS`. The hook sync-test
  (I-4) and the scrub logic still land with #23.
- `PyYAML>=6` added to runtime dependencies. YAML parsing uses `yaml.safe_load`.

No version bump: this PR adds importable machinery but does not yet produce
output bytes. Per the bump policy above, the next byte-affecting story will
carry the bump.

- `rules/jitter.py` carries the v1 design (PRD section 9b) and a

fix(sanitizer): apply /simplify review pass on config loader (#19)

Applies the 12 confirmed findings from a /simplify review of PR #29
(YAML config loader, I-3 replacement-leak guard, and pattern constants).
All correctness bugs were caught by either the line-by-line angle, the
removed-behavior auditor, or the Python-pitfall specialist; the cleanups
by the simplification/reuse/efficiency/altitude angles.

Security correctness
--------------------

PEM private-key regex now catches `ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY` (standard
PKCS#8 encrypted PEM — the output of `openssl pkcs8` and passphrase-
protected `ssh-keygen`). Previously only the unencrypted variants
matched, so an encrypted private key in session output could slip past
both the scrub layer (#23) and the residual scan (#24) — exactly the
catastrophic-class failure PRD §3 says must fail-closed.

Config schema correctness
-------------------------

- `version` is now type-checked. YAML `version: true` parses to Python
  `True`; without the isinstance gate `True == 1` silently accepted it
  and the loader returned `Config(version=True, ...)`. Same for
  `version: 1.0` (float). Loader now requires int that is not bool.

- `extra_secret_patterns` now mirrors path/identifier semantics: bare
  strings are literals (re.escape'd), `re:`-prefixed strings are
  regex. The earlier loader compiled bare strings raw, so `pattern:
  "C++"` silently became a regex with a quantifier. Shared helper
  `_split_regex_prefix` keeps the two code paths from drifting.

- `extra_secret_patterns: [{pattern: "re:"}]` now raises ConfigError
  with the same "empty regex after re: prefix" guard `_compile_rule`
  has for paths/identifiers. The earlier loader compiled an empty
  regex which matches every position, tripping the I-3 guard against
  every replacement value in the config.

- I-3 leak guard no longer skips the self-rule comparison. A rule
  whose own `replace` contains its own `match` (e.g., `{match:
  "/home/user", replace: "/home/user-redacted"}`) is non-
  idempotent: a second pass re-substitutes, and the sidecar broadcasts
  the original pattern. Now rejected with a focused error message
  ("not idempotent").

- Empty YAML sections (`paths:`/`identifiers:`/`extra_secret_patterns:`
  with no value, which `yaml.safe_load` parses to `None`) are now
  treated as empty lists, matching how `options:` already handles
  None. Previously raised `ConfigError("paths must be a list, got
  NoneType")` for an ergonomic shape that means "no rules".

Immutability and contract
-------------------------

- `Config` field lists are converted to tuples in `__post_init__`.
  `@dataclass(frozen=True)` blocks attribute reassignment but not list
  mutation; with mutable lists, downstream code could
  `config.paths.append(...)` after `load_config` returned and bypass
  the I-3 guard. Tuples preserve iteration ergonomics while blocking
  the bypass.

- `Rule` and `ExtraSecretPattern` validate `compiled.pattern` and
  `is_regex` against `pattern` in `__post_init__`. Both types are
  exported via `__all__`; without the check, a direct
  `Rule(pattern="/foo", compiled=re.compile("BAR"))` would lie about
  itself and pass through the I-3 guard miscompared. The same check
  reasserts the field invariant when called via the loader, at
  near-zero cost.

CLI exit-code contract
----------------------

- `load_config` now expands `~` so a quoted `--config
  '~/.ccs-sanitize.yaml'` from the CLI works instead of raising
  FileNotFoundError against a literal tilde.

- Non-UTF-8 config files and other `OSError` from `read_text` are now
  wrapped in `ConfigError` so the CLI's planned ConfigError → exit-3
  mapping catches them. Previously a Windows UTF-16-saved config
  surfaced as a bare `UnicodeDecodeError` and bypassed the docstring
  contract.

Performance / hygiene
---------------------

- `_check_replacement_leak` now uses a module-level `_BUILTIN_COMPILED`
  list instead of recompiling SECRET_PATTERNS on every call. The
  table compiles at module import, so a future typo in a vendored
  or batch pattern surfaces at import time, not on first config load.

- `ConfigOptions` defaults are owned by the dataclass; `_build_options`
  forwards only YAML-present keys instead of restating each default.
  Previously the defaults lived in both places and could drift if the
  dataclass default changed.

Deferred
--------

The following are real but the right fix lives elsewhere:

- ReDoS risk on user-supplied regex — needs subprocess timeout or
  pattern-complexity heuristic, both heavy. Accept residual risk for
  v0 and document in PRD if it becomes an actual concern.
- `Rule.replace` backreference validation — only meaningful when #21
  / #22 wires `re.sub`; defer to those PRs.
- `SECRET_PATTERNS` storage shape (str vs compiled) and `Rule` /
  `ExtraSecretPattern` unification — wait for #23 to determine what
  shape the scrub layer wants.
- Sidecar placeholder category field on `Rule` — wait for #25 design.
- ConfigError → subclasses for finer CLI diagnostics — wait for #26
  to see if it actually adds value.
- `config.py` → `rules/secrets.py` import direction — preventative,
  defer until #23 lands actual scrub code there.
- Landing the I-4 hook sync-test now rather than waiting for #23 —
  the PRD assigns that test explicitly to #23 and the architect's
  D-6 decision keeps the boundary clean.

Test suite
----------

44 passed, 0 failed, no skips (the smoke test in test_cli_smoke.py
still skips when the entry point isn't on PATH; that's the only skip
across the package). 13 new tests cover:

- bare `pattern: "C++"` is literal in extras (not regex)
- `pattern: "re:"` in extras raises (empty regex after prefix)
- PEM `ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY` pattern matches
- `version: true` / `1.0` / `"1"` rejected
- I-3 self-rule-replace-contains-own-match rejected
- Config.{paths,identifiers,extra_secret_patterns} are tuples
- `~` expansion works
- Non-UTF-8 input raises ConfigError
- Empty YAML sections (None) treated as empty
- Options defaults only apply when key omitted
- Rule/ExtraSecretPattern construction with mismatched compiled raises

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
Yes — but the answer has a wrinkle.

**The current state**
- `.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py` has **zero PEM coverage** today. Its `SECRET_PATTERNS` is API tokens only (anthropic, openai, github, AWS, GCP keys).
- My fix only widened the sanitizer's BATCH_PATTERNS regex to include `ENCRYPTED `. The hook never had PEM at all.
- PRD §9's architecture (Tier 2 = "sanitizer-only, patterns the hook never had to catch") was a design call — but PEM in particular is a poor fit for that boundary because `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `openssl pkcs8`, and `ssh-keygen` output are exactly the kind of live tool output the hook is designed to guard against. The hook's purpose is "block Claude from reasoning about tool output with secrets" — a PEM dump is the catastrophic case.

**My recommendation: yes, but rethink the layering**

Adding PEM only to the hook (not touching the sanitizer) is the easy answer. But there's a cleaner version that respects the I-4 sync invariant we're about to set up in #23:

- **Move PEM (with the ENCRYPTED variant) from `BATCH_PATTERNS` → `VENDORED_PATTERNS`** in `rules/secrets.py`.
- **Add the same PEM pattern to the hook's `SECRET_PATTERNS`** at the corresponding position.
- **Update PRD §9** to reflect that Tier 1 now includes PEM (the original carve-out was "Tier 1 mirrors what the hook already had" — we're expanding what the hook has).
- Add a fixture in `.claude/hooks/tests/fixtures/` for an ENCRYPTED PEM block to exercise the new pattern.

That preserves the architectural invariant ("Tier 1 = hook's set, byte-for-byte"). The alternative (PEM only in the hook, also in Tier 2 of the sanitizer) creates a third tier of "in hook but separately in sanitizer-Tier-2" — fine but awkward, and the future I-4 sync test would have to special-case it.

**The broader question worth flagging:**
The same logic arguably applies to **bearer tokens, JWTs, and DB connection strings with passwords** — those also appear in live tool output (`curl -v`, app logs from `tail`, env dumps). Whether all of Tier 2 should migrate to the hook is a real PRD-level decision; PEM is the most defensible "this should have always been in the hook" of the bunch.

Want me to:
1. **Just PEM** — move PEM → Tier 1, add to hook, update PRD §9, add fixture (small, surgical PR)?
2. **All of Tier 2** — same migration for JWT/bearer/conn-string/Slack too (bigger reshape, needs PRD update on the §9 Tier rationale)?
3. **Hold** — keep the carve-out as-is; sanitizer is the sole line of defense for PEM/JWT/bearer/etc.

I'd recommend **option 1** — PEM is the strongest single argument and a one-PR fix without forcing a broader rethink. Options 2 and 3 are then independent decisions you can revisit when #23 lands.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tests for the secrets-protection hooks. Stdlib only.

Run directly:
    python3 .claude/hooks/tests/test_hooks.py
or via pytest. Each case pipes a synthetic event fixture into the matching
hook and asserts the resulting block/deny/allow decision. The known-bad
fixtures contain only fake, clearly-synthetic credential patterns.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

HOOKS_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FIXTURES_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures"
PRE_HOOK = HOOKS_DIR / "block_secret_reads.py"
POST_HOOK = HOOKS_DIR / "detect_secrets_in_output.py"


def run_hook(hook_path: Path, event_text: str) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(hook_path)],
        input=event_text,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=10,
    )
    return result.stdout


def load_fixture(name: str) -> str:
    return (FIXTURES_DIR / name).read_text()


def hook_for(event_text: str) -> Path:
    name = json.loads(event_text).get("hook_event_name")
    return PRE_HOOK if name == "PreToolUse" else POST_HOOK


class HookBlockingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def _decision(self, fixture: str) -> dict:
        text = load_fixture(fixture)
        out = run_hook(hook_for(text), text)
        return json.loads(out) if out.strip() else {}

    def test_credential_env_read_denied(self):
        d = self._decision("block_credential_env.json")
        self.assertEqual(
            d.get("hookSpecificOutput", {}).get("permissionDecision"), "deny"
        )
        self.assertIn(
            "credential source",
            d["hookSpecificOutput"]["permissionDecisionReason"],
        )

    def test_raw_session_read_denied(self):
        d = self._decision("block_raw_session_read.json")
        self.assertEqual(
            d.get("hookSpecificOutput", {}).get("permissionDecision"), "deny"
        )
        self.assertIn(
            "raw Claude Code session",
            d["hookSpecificOutput"]["permissionDecisionReason"],
        )

    def test_secret_in_output_blocked(self):
        d = self._decision("block_secret_in_output.json")
        self.assertEqual(d.get("decision"), "block")
        self.assertIn("anthropic-key", d.get("reason", ""))

    def test_fixture_read_allowed(self):
        # A fixtures/ jsonl read is legitimate and must NOT be blocked.
        self.assertEqual(self._decision("allow_fixture_read.json"), {})

    def test_bash_tail_session_allowed(self):
        # Bash is excluded from the raw-session block by design, so the
        # documented `tail -f ~/.claude/projects/...` workflow still works.
        self.assertEqual(self._decision("allow_bash_tail_session.json"), {})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PostToolUse hook: block Claude from reasoning about tool output with secrets.

PostToolUse cannot redact non-MCP tool output inline. Instead, this hook uses
the detect-and-block pattern: if the tool response contains a known API key
or token pattern, it emits `{"decision": "block", "reason": ...}` so Claude
Code surfaces a block signal alongside the result and Claude knows not to
echo, summarize, or otherwise act on the leaked value.

Caveat: PostToolUse fires AFTER the tool has executed. The raw output is
already persisted in the session JSONL, and Claude still technically receives
the tool_result in-session. This hook prevents further propagation (summaries,
follow-up prompts quoting the value) but does NOT prevent the on-disk leak.
The PreToolUse block_secret_reads.py hook is the primary defense against
on-disk leakage; this is a secondary guard.

Cross-platform: stdlib only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys

SECRET_PATTERNS: list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], str]] = [
    (re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"), "anthropic-key"),
    (re.compile(r"sk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"), "openai-project-key"),
    (re.compile(r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}"), "openai-key-legacy"),
    (re.compile(r"ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}"), "github-pat-classic"),
    (re.compile(r"github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{40,}"), "github-pat-fine"),
    (re.compile(r"AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}"), "aws-access-key-id"),
    (re.compile(r"AIza[A-Za-z0-9_-]{35}"), "gcp-api-key"),
]

DENY_REASON_TEMPLATE = (
    "Blocked by claude-code-sessions secrets-protection hook "
    "(.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py). "
    "Tool output contained a value matching a known credential pattern: {kinds}. "
    "Claude is being prevented from reasoning about this output to avoid further "
    "propagation (e.g. echoing in summaries). "
    "IMPORTANT: the raw value has already been persisted in the session JSONL "
    "because PostToolUse fires after tool execution. Rotate any key that may have "
    "leaked and see CLAUDE.md (Security posture) and .claude/hooks/README.md for "
    "full remediation steps."
)


def stringify_response(resp: object) -> str:
    """Coerce tool_response (dict, list, str, etc.) into a single searchable string."""
    if isinstance(resp, str):
        return resp
    try:
        return json.dumps(resp, default=str)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return str(resp)


def find_secret_kinds(text: str) -> list[str]:
    kinds: list[str] = []
    for pattern, label in SECRET_PATTERNS:
        if pattern.search(text):
            kinds.append(label)
    return kinds


def emit_block(reason: str) -> None:
    payload = {"decision": "block", "reason": reason}
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(payload))


def main() -> int:
    try:
        event = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(
            f"detect_secrets_in_output: failed to parse hook event JSON: {e}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 0

    response = event.get("tool_response")
    if response is None:
        return 0

    text = stringify_response(response)
    kinds = find_secret_kinds(text)
    if kinds:
        reason = DENY_REASON_TEMPLATE.format(kinds=", ".join(sorted(set(kinds))))
        emit_block(reason)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tests for the secrets-protection hooks. Stdlib only.

Run directly:
    python3 .claude/hooks/tests/test_hooks.py
or via pytest. Each case pipes a synthetic event fixture into the matching
hook and asserts the resulting block/deny/allow decision. The known-bad
fixtures contain only fake, clearly-synthetic credential patterns.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

HOOKS_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FIXTURES_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures"
PRE_HOOK = HOOKS_DIR / "block_secret_reads.py"
POST_HOOK = HOOKS_DIR / "detect_secrets_in_output.py"


def run_hook(hook_path: Path, event_text: str) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(hook_path)],
        input=event_text,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=10,
    )
    return result.stdout


def load_fixture(name: str) -> str:
    return (FIXTURES_DIR / name).read_text()


def hook_for(event_text: str) -> Path:
    name = json.loads(event_text).get("hook_event_name")
    return PRE_HOOK if name == "PreToolUse" else POST_HOOK


class HookBlockingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def _decision(self, fixture: str) -> dict:
        text = load_fixture(fixture)
        out = run_hook(hook_for(text), text)
        return json.loads(out) if out.strip() else {}

    def test_credential_env_read_denied(self):
        d = self._decision("block_credential_env.json")
        self.assertEqual(
            d.get("hookSpecificOutput", {}).get("permissionDecision"), "deny"
        )
        self.assertIn(
            "credential source",
            d["hookSpecificOutput"]["permissionDecisionReason"],
        )

    def test_raw_session_read_denied(self):
        d = self._decision("block_raw_session_read.json")
        self.assertEqual(
            d.get("hookSpecificOutput", {}).get("permissionDecision"), "deny"
        )
        self.assertIn(
            "raw Claude Code session",
            d["hookSpecificOutput"]["permissionDecisionReason"],
        )

    def test_secret_in_output_blocked(self):
        d = self._decision("block_secret_in_output.json")
        self.assertEqual(d.get("decision"), "block")
        self.assertIn("anthropic-key", d.get("reason", ""))

    def test_fixture_read_allowed(self):
        # A fixtures/ jsonl read is legitimate and must NOT be blocked.
        self.assertEqual(self._decision("allow_fixture_read.json"), {})

    def test_bash_tail_session_allowed(self):
        # Bash is excluded from the raw-session block by design, so the
        # documented `tail -f ~/.claude/projects/...` workflow still works.
        self.assertEqual(self._decision("allow_bash_tail_session.json"), {})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

# Changelog — `claude-code-sessions-sanitizer`

All notable changes to this package will be documented here. The version
recorded in every `.scrubbed` sidecar (`sanitizer_version:` field, PRD section 10)
references this file.

## Bump policy

**Bump on any change that could alter the produced output bytes.** That
includes, non-exhaustively:

- New or modified path / identifier / secret rules.
- New entries in `VENDORED_PATTERNS` or `BATCH_PATTERNS`.
- Any change to the line-loop, the structural traversal skip-list, or the
  set of stripped line types.
- Changes to JSON serialization parameters (separators, key order, ASCII
  escaping) or the sidecar emission contract.
- Bug fixes in a regex that change which inputs match.

A bug fix that does **not** change which inputs match (e.g., refactoring a
helper, fixing an error message) does not require a bump.

The rule is conservative because the PRD's determinism contract — "same input
+ same config → byte-identical output" — only holds *within* a sanitizer
version. Downstream consumers (the fixture-validator, sibling projects) gate
on the sidecar's `sanitizer_version`. If the bytes change without the version,
the contract is meaningless.

Use semver: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.

- `PATCH` — bug fix that changes which inputs match a rule (no rule added or
  removed; no config-surface change).
- `MINOR` — new rule, new pattern, new CLI flag, new sidecar field. Backward
  compatible at the config-surface level.
- `MAJOR` — sidecar format change, config schema break, removal of a built-in
  pattern, or any change requiring re-running the sanitizer on previously
  scrubbed sessions.

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed (review pass on issue #19)
- **PEM private-key pattern now catches `ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY`** (standard
  PKCS#8 encrypted PEM, the output of `openssl pkcs8` and passphrase-
  protected `ssh-keygen`). Previously only the unencrypted variants matched,
  so an encrypted private key in session output could slip past both scrubs
  and the residual scan.
- `extra_secret_patterns` now mirror path/identifier rule semantics: bare
  strings are treated as literals (`re.escape`'d), `re:`-prefixed strings
  are compiled as regex. The earlier loader compiled bare strings raw, so
  `pattern: "C++"` silently became a regex with a quantifier.
- `extra_secret_patterns` with `pattern: "re:"` now raises `ConfigError`
  (same guard `_compile_rule` has for paths/identifiers). The previous
  loader accepted the empty regex, which matches every position and would
  trip the I-3 guard against every rule.
- `version` is now type-checked. YAML `version: true` (parses to Python
  `True`) and `version: 1.0` were silently accepted because Python treats
  `True == 1` and `1.0 == 1`; the loader now requires an `int` that is
  not a `bool`.
- I-3 replacement-leak guard no longer skips the self-rule comparison,
  so a rule whose own `replace` contains its own `match` (a non-
  idempotent rule that would leak the original pattern through the
  sidecar) is rejected with a focused error.
- `Config` field lists (`paths`, `identifiers`, `extra_secret_patterns`)
  are converted to tuples in `__post_init__`. `@dataclass(frozen=True)`
  blocks attribute reassignment but not list mutation; with mutable lists,
  downstream code could `config.paths.append(...)` after `load_config`
  returned, bypassing the I-3 guard.
- `load_config(path)` now expands `~` in the input path. Quoted
  `--config '~/.ccs-sanitize.yaml'` from the CLI was previously raising
  `FileNotFoundError` against a literal tilde.
- `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` errors and other `OSError` from the read
  step are now wrapped in `ConfigError` so the CLI's (eventual)
  `ConfigError` → exit 3 mapping catches them; previously a Windows
  UTF-16-saved config would surface as a bare `UnicodeDecodeError` and
  bypass the documented exit-code contract.
- Empty YAML sections — `paths:`/`identifiers:`/`extra_secret_patterns:`
  with no value (parses to `None`) — are now treated as empty lists,
  matching how `options:` already handles `None`. Previously the loader
  raised `ConfigError("paths must be a list, got NoneType")` for an
  ergonomic shape that should mean "no rules".
- `_check_replacement_leak` now uses a module-level `_BUILTIN_COMPILED`
  table instead of recompiling `SECRET_PATTERNS` on every call. The
  table compiles at module import, so a future typo in a vendored or
  batch pattern surfaces at import time, not on first config load.
- `ConfigOptions` defaults are owned by the dataclass; `_build_options`
  forwards only YAML-present keys instead of restating each default.
  Previously the defaults lived in both places and could drift.

  `is_regex` are consistent with `pattern` in `__post_init__`. Both
  types are exported via `__all__`; without the check, a direct
  `Rule(pattern="/foo", compiled=re.compile("BAR"))` would lie about
  itself and pass through the I-3 guard miscompared.

above, including bare-string-as-literal behavior, encrypted PEM
matching, and tuple-vs-list immutability.

  per PRD §12 schema and returns a typed `Config` (with `Rule`, `ExtraSecretPattern`,
  `ConfigOptions` sub-types). Surfaces `ConfigError` (a `ValueError` subclass) for
  malformed YAML, schema violations, invalid regex, attempts to add unknown keys, and
  I-3 replacement-leak failures. A missing file surfaces as `FileNotFoundError` so the
  CLI (#26) can map it to exit 1 distinct from `ConfigError` → exit 3 (PRD §11).

def test_version_bool_rejected(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """``version: true`` in YAML parses to Python ``True``; without the
    isinstance gate ``True == 1`` would silently accept it (and the
    sidecar would later serialize a bool)."""
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="version must be an integer"):
        load_config(_write(tmp_path, "version: true\n"))


def test_version_float_rejected(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """``version: 1.0`` compares equal to ``1`` but is a float; reject so
    the sidecar's sanitizer_version stays integer-typed."""
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="version must be an integer"):
        load_config(_write(tmp_path, "version: 1.0\n"))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PreToolUse hook: block reads of files likely to contain credentials, and of
raw Claude Code session transcripts.

Receives the PreToolUse event JSON on stdin. Denies the tool call when the
target file path (or Bash command argument) matches:

1. Known credential files: .env variants, shell rc files, SSH private keys,
   and named secrets files. (Checked for file tools, search tools, and Bash.)
2. Raw session JSONL under ~/.claude/projects/. (Checked for Read/Edit/
   NotebookEdit/Grep/Glob only — NOT Bash, so `tail -f`/`ls` demos and the
   sanitizer CLI still work.) This enforces this repo's posture: read sample
   data from fixtures/, never an unsanitized session transcript.

Emits a JSON decision on stdout and exits 0 (the modern pattern); exit 2
+ stderr is the legacy fallback but not used here.

Cross-platform: stdlib only, no shell dependencies.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import PurePath

# The BLOCKED_BASENAMES set and the CREDENTIAL_TOKEN_PATTERNS list must stay in
# sync — they express the same credential-file list in two matching contexts
# (exact basename vs. substring-in-command-or-pattern). Update both together.
BLOCKED_BASENAMES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        ".env",
        ".envrc",
        "credentials",
        "credentials.json",
        "secrets.yaml",
        "secrets.yml",
        "secrets.json",
        ".bashrc",
        ".bash_profile",
        ".profile",
        ".zshrc",
        ".zshenv",
        ".zprofile",
        "id_rsa",
        "id_ed25519",
        "id_ecdsa",
        "id_dsa",
    }
)

BLOCKED_SUFFIXES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({".pem"})

CREDENTIAL_TOKEN_PATTERNS: list[str] = [
    r"\.env(\b|[._-][A-Za-z0-9_-]+)",
    r"\.envrc\b",
    r"credentials\.json\b",
    r"secrets\.ya?ml\b",
    r"secrets\.json\b",
    r"\.bashrc\b",
    r"\.bash_profile\b",
    r"\.profile\b",
    r"\.zshrc\b",
    r"\.zshenv\b",
    r"\.zprofile\b",
    r"\bid_rsa\b",
    r"\bid_ed25519\b",
    r"\bid_ecdsa\b",
    r"\bid_dsa\b",
    r"\.pem\b",
]
CREDENTIAL_TOKEN_REGEX = re.compile("|".join(CREDENTIAL_TOKEN_PATTERNS), re.IGNORECASE)

FILE_PATH_TOOLS = {"Read", "Edit", "Write", "NotebookEdit"}
PATH_SEARCH_TOOLS = {"Grep", "Glob"}

# Raw-session block applies to the tools that pull file *contents* into context.
# Write is excluded (it overwrites, it doesn't surface existing content) and
# Bash is excluded by design (keeps `tail -f`/`ls` and the sanitizer CLI usable).
RAW_SESSION_FILE_TOOLS = {"Read", "Edit", "NotebookEdit"}

# ~/.claude/projects/ is where Claude Code writes raw, unsanitized session
# transcripts. Anything ending in .jsonl under that root is a raw session.
RAW_SESSION_ROOT = PurePath(os.path.expanduser("~")) / ".claude" / "projects"

DENY_REASON = (
    "Blocked by claude-code-sessions secrets-protection hook (.claude/hooks/block_secret_reads.py). "
    "This file is a likely credential source (.env, shell rc, SSH key, or named secrets file). "
    "Reading it would persist its contents in the Claude Code session JSONL. "
    "If you need to verify the file exists, use `test -f <path>`. "
    "See CLAUDE.md (Security posture) and .claude/hooks/README.md for the full policy."
)

RAW_SESSION_DENY_REASON = (
    "Blocked by claude-code-sessions secrets-protection hook (.claude/hooks/block_secret_reads.py). "
    "This is a raw Claude Code session transcript under ~/.claude/projects/. Reading it into context "
    "risks surfacing prompts, file contents, command output, or secrets from an unsanitized session. "
    "Per this repo's security posture (CLAUDE.md), read sample data from fixtures/ instead, or run the "
    "sanitizer to produce a scrubbed copy. See .claude/hooks/README.md for the policy."
)


def path_is_blocked(path_str: str) -> bool:
    if not path_str:
        return False
    p = PurePath(path_str)
    name = p.name
    if name in BLOCKED_BASENAMES:
        return True
    if p.suffix in BLOCKED_SUFFIXES:
        return True
    if name.startswith((".env.", ".env-", ".env_")):
        return True
    return False


def path_is_raw_session(path_str: str) -> bool:
    if not path_str:
        return False
    p = PurePath(os.path.expanduser(path_str))
    if p.suffix != ".jsonl":
        return False
    return RAW_SESSION_ROOT in p.parents


def bash_command_is_blocked(command: str) -> bool:
    if not command:
        return False
    return CREDENTIAL_TOKEN_REGEX.search(command) is not None


def check(event: dict) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    tool_name = event.get("tool_name", "")
    tool_input = event.get("tool_input") or {}

    if tool_name in FILE_PATH_TOOLS:
        path = tool_input.get("file_path") or tool_input.get("notebook_path") or ""
        if path_is_blocked(path):
            return True, f"{DENY_REASON} (path: {path})"
        if tool_name in RAW_SESSION_FILE_TOOLS and path_is_raw_session(path):
            return True, f"{RAW_SESSION_DENY_REASON} (path: {path})"

    if tool_name in PATH_SEARCH_TOOLS:
        path = tool_input.get("path") or ""
        pattern = tool_input.get("pattern") or ""
        if path and path_is_blocked(path):
            return True, f"{DENY_REASON} (search path: {path})"
        if path and path_is_raw_session(path):
            return True, f"{RAW_SESSION_DENY_REASON} (search path: {path})"
        if pattern and CREDENTIAL_TOKEN_REGEX.search(pattern):
            return True, f"{DENY_REASON} (search pattern targets credential file: {pattern})"

    if tool_name == "Bash":
        command = tool_input.get("command") or ""
        if bash_command_is_blocked(command):
            return True, f"{DENY_REASON} (command: {command[:200]})"

    return False, ""


def emit_decision(decision: str, reason: str) -> None:
    payload = {
        "hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
            "permissionDecision": decision,
            "permissionDecisionReason": reason,
        }
    }
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(payload))


def main() -> int:
    try:
        event = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        # Fail closed: this is a security-critical PreToolUse hook. If we can't
        # parse the event we cannot confirm the call is safe, so deny rather
        # than allow through a malformed event of unknown provenance.
        print(
            f"block_secret_reads: failed to parse hook event JSON, denying by default: {e}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    blocked, reason = check(event)
    if blocked:
        emit_decision("deny", reason)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

feat(hooks)!: promote PEM private-key to Tier 1 (hook + VENDORED)

PEM private-key armor was previously a Tier-2 (BATCH_PATTERNS) entry
in the sanitizer and was not in the hook at all. The hook's purpose
is to block Claude from reasoning about live tool output containing
credentials; cat'ing an SSH private key, `openssl pkcs8` output, and
passphrase-protected `ssh-keygen` output are the catastrophic-class
case the hook exists for. The architect's original Tier-1/Tier-2
boundary framed Tier 2 as "patterns the hook never had to catch" —
but for PEM specifically that framing was an oversight, not a
property of the world.

Changes
-------

- `.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py`: append
  `pem-private-key` to `SECRET_PATTERNS`. Same regex shape used in the
  sanitizer (includes the `ENCRYPTED` PKCS#8 variant from PR #29's
  review fix).

- `tooling/sanitizer/src/ccs_sanitize/rules/secrets.py`: move the
  `pem-private-key` tuple from `BATCH_PATTERNS` to the end of
  `VENDORED_PATTERNS`. Order matches the hook's `SECRET_PATTERNS`
  element-wise so the I-4 sync test that lands in #23 can compare
  positionally.

- `.claude/specs/prd-sanitizer.md` §9: Tier-1 example list grows by
  the PEM entry; Tier-2 entry table loses PEM. Narrative updated to
  "patterns the hook does not currently catch" (no longer "never had
  to catch") and to reference the backlog issue tracking whether the
  remaining Tier-2 patterns (bearer, JWT, conn-string-pw, slack)
  should also promote.

- `.claude/hooks/tests/fixtures/block_pem_private_key.json`: new
  fixture; synthetic ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY block in a Bash
  `tool_response` payload. Body content is obviously fake to keep the
  fixture-of-known-bad-input invariant the rest of the fixtures
  follow.

- `.claude/hooks/tests/test_hooks.py`: new `test_pem_private_key_blocked`
  case wires the fixture through and asserts `decision == block` with
  `pem-private-key` in the reason. Six hook tests now pass.

- `tooling/sanitizer/tests/test_config.py`: existing
  `test_pem_pattern_catches_encrypted_private_key` updated to look
  in `VENDORED_PATTERNS` (was BATCH); new
  `test_pem_pattern_is_in_tier_1_not_tier_2` pins the partition so a
  future regression that re-tiers PEM trips the test, not the I-4
  sync test alone.

Out of scope
------------

The broader "should all of Tier 2 land in the hook?" question
(bearer tokens, JWTs, DB connection strings with passwords, Slack
tokens — all of which appear in live tool output too) is tracked
separately in a backlog issue. PEM had the strongest "this should
have always been in the hook" argument; the others need architect
review before promotion.

The `!` in the commit type marks this as a Tier-1 reshape —
`BATCH_PATTERNS` shrank by one entry. Tests on this branch and on
PR #29 (`feature/19-config-loader`, which still has PEM in BATCH)
both pass; PR #29's CHANGELOG entry for the ENCRYPTED widening is
preserved and the body of this commit carries the partition move.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- Updates PRD §9 to reflect the partition (and reframes the Tier-2 rationale from "patterns the hook never had to catch" to "patterns the hook does not currently catch" — the original framing was an oversight, not a property of the world).

PR #29's review pass added the `ENCRYPTED ` variant to the existing PEM regex but kept it in Tier 2. ### Why this is a separate PR

PR #29's scope is "config loader + I-3 guard + initial pattern constants". Reshuffling the Tier 1/2 partition is a separate concern that touches `.claude/hooks/` (security boundary) and PRD §9 (architecture). Keeping these atomic makes the architect-validated decisions easier to track later.

### Branch base

This PR targets `feature/19-config-loader` so the diff shows only the partition move while #29 is open. When #29 merges to main, GitHub will retarget the base automatically and the diff stays clean.

### Out of scope (tracked separately)

A follow-up issue will track the broader option-2 question: should the remaining Tier-2 patterns (`bearer-token`, `jwt`, `conn-string-pw`, `slack-token`) also promote to the hook? Each of those appears in live tool output (`curl -v`, app logs from `tail`, env dumps) so the same argument applies in principle, but the case is weaker per-pattern and the architect should weigh in before promotion.

- [x] Hook tests pass: `python3 .claude/hooks/tests/test_hooks.py` — 6 cases (was 5; new `test_pem_private_key_blocked`).

- [x] PRD §9 narrative and code blocks updated.
- [x] CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]` documents the reshape.

The sanitizer's Tier 1/2 partition changes: `BATCH_PATTERNS` shrinks by one entry, `VENDORED_PATTERNS` grows by one entry. `SECRET_PATTERNS = VENDORED + BATCH` is byte-identical (same patterns, same total). ## Background

PR #31 promoted `pem-private-key` from the sanitizer's Tier-2 (`BATCH_PATTERNS`, sanitizer-only) to Tier 1 (`VENDORED_PATTERNS`, mirrored in `.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py`). The argument was: PEM private keys appear in live tool output (`cat ~/.ssh/id_*`, `openssl pkcs8`, passphrase-protected `ssh-keygen`), which is exactly the case the live hook exists to guard against — not just an at-rest session-file concern.

PR #31's PRD update also reframed the Tier-2 rationale: from "patterns the hook never had to catch" to "patterns the hook does not currently catch". The first framing was an architectural oversight; the second is a status quo that should be revisited per pattern.

This issue tracks the broader question: **should the remaining Tier-2 patterns also promote to the hook?** The four patterns:

| Pattern | Lives in live tool output? | Real-world example |
|---|---|---|
| `bearer-token` (`<REDACTED:bearer-token>`) | Yes | `curl -v` showing request headers, `tail -f app.log` of an API server |
| `jwt` (`eyJ...eyJ...sig...`) | Yes | Same as above; JWTs in browser console output, decoded tokens from `jq` |
| `conn-string-pw` (`<REDACTED:conn-string-pw>host/db`) | Yes | `env`, `cat` of a config file, ORM startup logs |
| `slack-token` (`xox[baprs]-...`) | Yes | `env`, app config dumps, webhook test outputs |

## Trade-offs (per-pattern analysis from chat)

**Pro (general):** The hook fires on `PostToolUse` for tool output. The block decision prevents Claude from summarizing or echoing the leaked value into follow-up prompts — secondary propagation prevention. Adding more patterns means catching more credential shapes in that window.

**Pro (subtle):** The same patterns are already in the sanitizer's Tier 2. Promotion to Tier 1 is "free" in the sense that the I-4 sync test (lands with #23) would gate the duplication automatically.

**Con (general):** Each new pattern has a false-positive surface. A `bearer-token` regex matches in the wrong context (a doc string mentioning `<REDACTED:bearer-token>`?) and the hook noisily blocks. The hook is a secondary guard — the raw value is already in the session JSONL — so over-blocking has user-experience cost without security gain.

**Con (per-pattern judgments to validate):**
- **`bearer-token`**: The regex `(?i)authorization:\s*bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` is specific enough that false positives are likely rare. Probably promotable. Strongest case after PEM.
- **`jwt`**: The regex `eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}` matches the JWT shape but doesn't decode. A JWT in a developer's debug output is legitimate read material; over-blocking impedes debugging. Possibly promotable but should consider.
- **`conn-string-pw`**: Specific shape (`scheme://user:pw@host`). False positives are rare. Probably promotable.
- **`slack-token`**: Specific Slack prefixes. False positives are rare. Probably promotable.

## What I (the model) said in chat

> The broader question worth flagging: The same logic arguably applies to bearer tokens, JWTs, and DB connection strings with passwords — those also appear in live tool output (`curl -v`, app logs from `tail`, env dumps). Whether all of Tier 2 should migrate to the hook is a real PRD-level decision; PEM is the most defensible "this should have always been in the hook" of the bunch.

> Want me to:
> 1. **Just PEM** — move PEM → Tier 1, add to hook, update PRD §9, add fixture (small, surgical PR)?
> 2. **All of Tier 2** — same migration for JWT/bearer/conn-string/Slack too (bigger reshape, needs PRD update on the §9 Tier rationale)?
> 3. **Hold** — keep the carve-out as-is; sanitizer is the sole line of defense for PEM/JWT/bearer/etc.

The user picked **option 1** (PEM only, shipped in PR #31). This issue tracks **option 2** for later evaluation.

## Architect-review questions

Before any of these patterns promote, the architect should weigh in on:

1. **Per-pattern false-positive rate** — for each of the four, what's the realistic UX impact of the hook blocking against a developer's `curl -v` or `tail -f app.log` output during debugging? Empirical signal: any of these patterns appear in this repo's own session JSONL transcripts in benign contexts?
2. **All-or-some** — promote all four together (clean reshape), or selectively (e.g., bearer-token first, JWT held back)?
3. **Tier 2 emptiness** — if all four promote, `BATCH_PATTERNS` is empty. Is that an architectural smell (the partition becomes vestigial)? Or do we keep BATCH around for future sanitizer-only additions where the hook coverage really isn't appropriate?
4. **Rename / collapse** — if the answer to #3 is "BATCH becomes vestigial", the architecture simplifies to one tier. Worth noting now so the I-4 sync test (#23) is designed accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria (if/when scoped for implementation)

- [ ] Architect review on the four patterns (recommendation: promote, hold, or partial promote)
- [ ] PRD §9 updated to reflect the final partition (and §9 / §3 / §11 narrative if Tier 2 collapses entirely)
- [ ] For each promoted pattern: add to hook's `SECRET_PATTERNS`, move out of `BATCH_PATTERNS`, add a hook fixture + test, update CHANGELOG
- [ ] Tier 1 element-wise ordering stays consistent with future I-4 sync test

## Related

- PR #31 (PEM promotion — the precedent for this evaluation)
- PR #29 (config loader + initial Tier-1/Tier-2 constants + I-3 leak guard)
- PRD §9 (Layer 3: secrets — the architectural source of truth)
- #23 (Layer 3 secrets implementation, where the I-4 sync test lands; that PR's design should anticipate whichever partition this issue resolves)

# Changelog — `claude-code-sessions-sanitizer`

All notable changes to this package will be documented here. The version
recorded in every `.scrubbed` sidecar (`sanitizer_version:` field, PRD section 10)
references this file.

## Bump policy

**Bump on any change that could alter the produced output bytes.** That
includes, non-exhaustively:

- New or modified path / identifier / secret rules.
- New entries in `VENDORED_PATTERNS` or `BATCH_PATTERNS`.
- Any change to the line-loop, the structural traversal skip-list, or the
  set of stripped line types.
- Changes to JSON serialization parameters (separators, key order, ASCII
  escaping) or the sidecar emission contract.
- Bug fixes in a regex that change which inputs match.

A bug fix that does **not** change which inputs match (e.g., refactoring a
helper, fixing an error message) does not require a bump.

The rule is conservative because the PRD's determinism contract — "same input
+ same config → byte-identical output" — only holds *within* a sanitizer
version. Downstream consumers (the fixture-validator, sibling projects) gate
on the sidecar's `sanitizer_version`. If the bytes change without the version,
the contract is meaningless.

Use semver: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.

- `PATCH` — bug fix that changes which inputs match a rule (no rule added or
  removed; no config-surface change).
- `MINOR` — new rule, new pattern, new CLI flag, new sidecar field. Backward
  compatible at the config-surface level.
- `MAJOR` — sidecar format change, config schema break, removal of a built-in
  pattern, or any change requiring re-running the sanitizer on previously
  scrubbed sessions.

# Changelog — `claude-code-sessions-sanitizer`

All notable changes to this package will be documented here. The version
recorded in every `.scrubbed` sidecar (`sanitizer_version:` field, PRD section 10)
references this file.

## Bump policy

**Bump on any change that could alter the produced output bytes.** That
includes, non-exhaustively:

- New or modified path / identifier / secret rules.
- New entries in `VENDORED_PATTERNS` or `BATCH_PATTERNS`.
- Any change to the line-loop, the structural traversal skip-list, or the
  set of stripped line types.
- Changes to JSON serialization parameters (separators, key order, ASCII
  escaping) or the sidecar emission contract.
- Bug fixes in a regex that change which inputs match.

A bug fix that does **not** change which inputs match (e.g., refactoring a
helper, fixing an error message) does not require a bump.

The rule is conservative because the PRD's determinism contract — "same input
+ same config → byte-identical output" — only holds *within* a sanitizer
version. Downstream consumers (the fixture-validator, sibling projects) gate
on the sidecar's `sanitizer_version`. If the bytes change without the version,
the contract is meaningless.

Use semver: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.

- `PATCH` — bug fix that changes which inputs match a rule (no rule added or
  removed; no config-surface change).
- `MINOR` — new rule, new pattern, new CLI flag, new sidecar field. Backward
  compatible at the config-surface level.
- `MAJOR` — sidecar format change, config schema break, removal of a built-in
  pattern, or any change requiring re-running the sanitizer on previously
  scrubbed sessions.

  `tool_use.id`, `thinking.signature`); the predicate now anchors them via

  by the transform and scrubbed by future rule layers instead of slipping
  through. `id`, `signature`, and `model` were removed from the
  unconditional bare-name set.

  any descendant of any field literally named `usage` at any depth — over-
  broad relative to the PRD section 6b B scope.

  number / array slipping past the strip-types gate and being silently
  walked), on missing `type` field, and on non-string `type` field. Each
  raises `PipelineError` with the source line number. PRD §11 says shape
  violations should abort.

  rather than the post-filter record index, so users can locate the bad
  line in their source file when blank lines precede it.
- `SubstitutionTable.__iter__` snapshots the entries via `list(...)` so
  concurrent `record()` calls during iteration do not raise
  `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`. A test pins
  the snapshot semantics.

## Summary

Reopen of #31 (auto-closed when its base `feature/19-config-loader` was deleted on the #29 merge).

Promotes `pem-private-key` from Tier 2 (`BATCH_PATTERNS`, sanitizer-only) to **Tier 1** (`VENDORED_PATTERNS`, mirrored verbatim in `.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py`). The hook had **zero PEM coverage** before this PR — so a live `cat ~/.ssh/id_*` or `openssl pkcs8` output (the catastrophic case the hook exists for) was not getting the block-from-further-propagation guard the hook gives API tokens.

The pattern regex shape is unchanged from PR #29's review fix (still includes the `ENCRYPTED ` PKCS#8 variant). This PR only moves where the pattern lives and adds the hook coverage.

## Changes

- `.claude/hooks/detect_secrets_in_output.py` — appended `pem-private-key` to `SECRET_PATTERNS`
- `tooling/sanitizer/src/ccs_sanitize/rules/secrets.py` — moved PEM from `BATCH_PATTERNS` to end of `VENDORED_PATTERNS` (positional)
- `.claude/specs/prd-sanitizer.md` §9 — Tier-1 example list grows; Tier-2 entry table loses PEM; narrative reframed
- `.claude/hooks/tests/fixtures/block_pem_private_key.json` — synthetic ENCRYPTED PEM fixture
- `.claude/hooks/tests/test_hooks.py` — `test_pem_private_key_blocked`
- `tooling/sanitizer/tests/test_config.py` — existing PEM test updated; new `test_pem_pattern_is_in_tier_1_not_tier_2` pins the partition
- `tooling/sanitizer/CHANGELOG.md` — Changed entry under `[Unreleased]`

Issue #32 tracks the broader option-2 evaluation (bearer-token / JWT / conn-string-pw / slack-token → hook).

## Test plan

- [x] Hook tests pass: `python3 .claude/hooks/tests/test_hooks.py` — 6 cases (was 5).
- [x] Sanitizer tests pass: 89 passed, 1 skipped.
- [x] No `cd` in subdirectories — all runs from repo root with absolute paths.

## Security review

- [x] **No raw session JSONL** — only the new synthetic fixture.
- [x] **No secrets** — fixture's `tool_response` is a synthetic PEM block matching the regex shape with `SYNTHETIC-FIXTURE-NOT-A-REAL-KEY-DO-NOT-USE` body.
- [x] **Closer read done** — touches `.claude/hooks/` (PR-required surface). The hook's `SECRET_PATTERNS` grows by one entry; existing behavior on the other 7 entries unchanged.

## Breaking changes

The sanitizer's Tier 1/2 partition changes: `BATCH_PATTERNS` shrinks by one entry, `VENDORED_PATTERNS` grows by one entry. `SECRET_PATTERNS = VENDORED + BATCH` is byte-identical (same patterns, same total). Any downstream code that iterates the full `SECRET_PATTERNS` is unaffected; code that branches on Tier (none today) would see PEM in the new Tier.

The `!` in the commit type marks this as a Tier-1 reshape.

### What happened along the way

- **#30 was already on main** by the time I started, so I only had work for #29 and #31.
- **#29 needed a rebase** against the new main (CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` conflict with #30's entries). Two rebase commits, two CHANGELOG conflicts resolved (#19 entries placed after #20 entries chronologically newest-first). Force-pushed, then squash-merged.

I rebased `feature/promote-pem-to-tier-1` onto the new main (`--onto origin/main bfaa3f2`), force-pushed, and opened a fresh **PR #33** with the same branch targeting `main`. Squash-merged.

### Final state on main

- **89 sanitizer tests pass, 1 expected skip** (the CLI smoke test that skips when the entry point isn't on PATH).
- **6 hook tests pass** (5 prior + new `test_pem_private_key_blocked`).

Local feature branches pruned. `main` is fast-forwarded. Stale PRs: #31 is closed-with-replacement (#33) — leaving it as a closed-with-link breadcrumb so future readers can see the redirect.
